Fantasticly unique RPG maker game.
I appluad the creator for the amount of custom assets that went into this experience, this is what I like to see with RM.
I was amazed to see that almost every enemy sprite you fought was different from the last, all with different names and personalities. With that said though yes this is an RPG maker game, and you do get those stock assets from time to time, this for the most part only includes sound effects and animations though. People who don't play RM games probably won't notice, but people who do after seeing so many unique things it's kind of a shame to hear the same punching sound you heard from 5 other RM games.
With that said, I liked just about everything this game had to offer.
+Fun characters.
+Interesting world.
+Great music, though some tracks could get under my skin if listened to for too long, overall it fits the world and really makes it feel weird and dirty... Which is a + in my books!
+Loads of secrets.
+Nice evironments and made like a 2D platformer, refreshing from an RM game.(Though this comes with a negative)
+Tons of things to interact with, this has to be one of the strongest things in the game for me, I had so much fun just exploring and trying out all kinds of things just to see how the people would react. You can get some very funny outcomes.
+Deep meaningful story, though at times hard to follow.
There are some negatives, they didn't ruin the game for me but they're there.
-The balancing in this game isn't all that well done, to be expected when it comes with so many characters. I like that different characters compliment each other with certain attacks or skills but most of that is rendered null after you get 2 certain characters.
-The game is made similar to that of a 2D platformer, though this is refreshing and works quite well,
it can be difficult to navigate certain areas, it's a bit difficult to remember which door it was you needed to go into, for me there was a lot of trial and error.
-Another thing is, this game leaves you kind of just... Out there, to do whatever you want and find your own way a lot, it doesn't always do great job on directing you on where to go, which is okay for the most part as exploration is always fun, but coupled with the last negative it can make finding where to go pretty difficult at times.
-I wish there were more choices! Sometimes there's choices, but when you try to do the right thing it leads to a bad thing so you're practically forced to do the wrong thing, and there were times I just didn't want to do what the game was making me do, though there were seemingly important choices before it there's none when I would like it most. Certain confrontations had me just hitting guard to see if I could progress the story when I lost, unfourtunately, nada.
Overall this was a very fun game to playthrough and I enjoyed my time with it, minor frustrations here and there but the story and sheer amount of interesting but weird.... and I mean WEIRD things just keep you going.

TRIP Runner2 is the hardcore version of this: you jump, slide, block, attack, dance, and do all kind of combinations (jump+slide, for example). You always need to evaluate what you need to do, and since there are so many options, the game quickly becomes challenging.
As if this wasn't enough, there's gold to collect and a score system. This helps giving you secondary objectives: you don't only look out at obstacles to avoid them, but also at gold to get it! This requires you to be even more watchful than this hard game asks you to be, and to sometimes willingfully put yourself in a dangerous situation. The gold allows you to unlock new levels, so if getting a "perfect" isn't a motivation to you, the new content should be.
I won't go into details about all the additional content (retro levels, alternative routes, the three level difficulties, chests...), but just keep in mind that if you love this game and its basic content (which you should!), then there's enough to keep you busy long after you finish the story.
The graphics are pretty good, the soundtrack is nice and the game itself is a constant challenge to your reflexes and agility.

What I didn't like the most is the level design. If you play for the first time, you will get stuck everywhere. Sometimes you need to shoot a crate somewhere to blow a hole in the wall or jump on top of a structure which is not self explanaitory. The game forces you to use weapons insead of lightsabre lot of times, because annoying snipers are everywhere. The problem on hardest difficulty is the lack of balance, it surely wasn't tested well. There are some very tough fights, the fight with Lando on Nar Shaddaa, where I was pulling my hair after trying for the hundredth time, while the main fights are quite easy. All in all a great game with some bad level design, 8/10 would recommend!

7. Игра высмеивает некоторые стереотипы и иногда смеётся над собой, но отсутствие предрассудков приводит к некоторым...Интересным моментам. ; )
Я очень рекомендую "Saints Row IV" тем, кто желют ощутить себя супергероями...Которые угоняют машины, спасают землю от пришельцев и матерятся с соратниками.
This game got me interested from the first trailer. I have not played in any part of the series. Despite the superficial resemblance to the "GTA" from the start it becomes clear that "Saints Row 4" is unique on several counts at once:
1. The story tells us that the plot though basically linear but the freedom of choice is present in a sufficient amount to have fun.
2. Humor is one of the pillars of this work. It is likely not everyone will appreciate but this "mad" humor hooked me too hard some times reminded of the game "Deadpool" (but "Saints Row IV"  related to it only with "super-heroism").
3. Super-powers! It is possible to jump high and freeze enemies, but you long to fly with a crash landing on passers-by. And throwing cars with telekinesis no one will ever be able to get tired!
4. The ability to control, steal and win in the trials the car is not quite new, but built-in acceleration and a change in body shape give scope for creativity.
5. There is a wide variety of tasks to perform which can be with their companions - a gang of "Saints".
6. The game has a multiplayer feature...Though the matching of super-partners are difficult to find, but work together to restore chaos more fun!
7. The game makes fun of some stereotypes and sometimes laughing at themselves but the lack of prejudice leads to some...Interesting moments. ; )
I highly recommend "Saints Row IV" for those who wants to feel like a superhero...Who steals cars, saves the earth from aliens and swearing with colleagues.

Tropico 3 is one of my favorite city builder games.
You play as El Presidente, the ruler of an unspecified little Caribbean island. You have to take care of your nation - build housing, farms, schools... You can earn money by exporting resources (surplus food, lumber, oil), manufactured goods (cigars, furniture) or through tourism (building hotels, venues, beach resorts etc).
In the meantime, you have to take care of the politics. Do not anger the US or USSR - you can't win if they invade you. In fact, they will support you if you have good relations. You can view the political preferences of every single citizen and tend to them, so they will vote for you. And those who won't? Bribe them or put them to the jail. Or don't hold the election at all. People will rebel, so make sure your soldiers are taken care of and loyal to you.
The whole game has a humorous atmosphere to mock the workings of banana republics and their dictator-presidents. It is a few years old (in the meantime, Tropico 4 and 5 came out), but it doesn't feel obsolete at all. The graphics are nice as well as  is the latino soundtrack.
I definitely recommend this game, especially now that it is on a huge discount sale.

In this age of hipster shovelware, it is a truly rare occasion to find an indie game that is easily worth an AAA price tag. Having learned of this jewel only recently, I was instantly hooked by its familiar yet original art style, addicting gameplay and just how polished it is (immersive soundtrack, actual character voice overs, etc). If you're not sure, there's a free playable demo at
.

Bright colors, amazing pixel animation, and some good voice work make this game a great homage to the Sega Genesis family of platformers (most specifically, Sonic the Hedgehog).
The games art style is uniquely stylish, something I don't see too often in the Indie Market. Gameplay wise, it's got the speed and fluidity of the Sega Genesis Sonic games with a traditional health system and combat akin to Gunstar Heroes. Speed through stages and take out bosses. It's as classic as classic can get. The soundtrack is catchy as hell, and you can buy it on steam for 7 bucks.
The game's main protagonists all play differently. Lilac plays just like Sonic combined with Ristar. She can boost, which allows her to move really fast and bounce off walls, and has the best melee combat moves in terms of damage, but most of the game's collectibles are far easier to collect using Carol or Milla.
Carol has faster melee attacks, but they deal less damage, and she can also scale walls. Carol receives her motorcycle by collecting cans of gasoline, which allows her to drive DIRECTLY UP WALLS and move faster.
Milla (only playable in Arcade Mode) is quite possibly the hardest character to play as. She has ranged projectiles and a shield that can reflect projectiles, but she has the lowest max health (just 4 slots).
The game's voice actors were actually pretty good, considering this is an indie game. The game's main heroines all relay their characters personalities without seeming forced, and this makes watching the game's cutscenes enjoyable. I particularly really enjoyed the performance of Xander Barriga, who voices Lord Brevon.
One negative most people seem to find with this game is it's difficulty level, as well as the bosses. I won't lie, the game gets pretty difficult towards the middle and the end requires having quite sharp reflexes, however, that's how most games should be in my opinion, and continuing doesn't restart you from the start of the stage anyway, so you have unlimited tries at whatever is besting you until you just give up. I can safely say, however, at no point in this game did I ever just quit it out of frustration. The game's difficulty kept me wanting to continue playing more than anything.
For 15 bucks, this is a really fun 2D Platformer. I really haven't had an indie game that has kept a huge grip on me like this one has. If you liked pretty much any genesis platformer, you'll probably love this game.

I enjoyed my playthrough of SR:HK-EE. I played the original full campaign as a custom build (assault-oriented with shotgun and backup assault rifle), then took that same character into the bonus campaign.
In terms of gameplay- SR:HK-EE is not much different than it's SR predecessors. It's turned-based combat using an action point system. Between combats, you have a lot of running your character around, looking for the next combat, equipment upgrades, money, or clues of some sort.
The story is good, with relatively well-developed player and non-player characters. There is a tremendous amount of reading involved in advancing the story. The average player who actually reads all the dialogue (as I did) will likely spend 2 to 3 times more reading than battling various baddies. Be warned.
This game is from a alternate timeline where Bioware stuck with making immersive story-driven rpg's instead of 3rd person shooters. Thank you Harebrained Schemes  for bringing it to us.

I would give it a pass if I could just play the game and not have to swim through oceans of pointlessly detailed neverending text. Even if I just click through the text, there is such an incredible amount it still takes a while to do that. Besides, who knows if I might miss something important by doing that and make further progression a nightmare without reading certain things. Who knows, who cares.

I think I like the characters and story of Shadowrun Hong Kong EE best of all the Shadowrun games. I think if you were going to only play one of these games, play Dragonfall. It's a tighter mix of gameplay, story and character development. But when you are hungry for more, or if you really prefer a stronger ratio of narrative in your RPGs, play Hong Kong. I enjoy the tactics combat, the RPG character progression choices, the story. All around a great game that you can really sink your teeth / dozens of hours into.

Maybe not quite as good as the Dragonfall campaign but Hong Kong is still a great cyberpunk RPG within an awesome, unique setting full of detail.
Would recommend playing through Dragonfall first and if you like that getting onto HK is a no-brainer.

Anyone here remember that video by Corridor Digital "Clock Blockers"?  That's more or less what this game is.
This has quickly reached high rankings in my favorite games. I love platformers, I love shooters, I love run&guns, I love puzzle games, and I love unique concepts. That's basically everything I love covered in a single title!  There are a few things I have complaints about however, but I'll get to those in a minute.
Pros:
- You can save yourself by going back in time and preventing the death from occuring
-The game can be played by almost anyone of any skill level, but there's harder challenges for those (like me) want a more difficult game
-Great sense of humor, and it doesn't even need to be vugar to be funny
-Replayability is very high. Each level contains various things to accomplish such as beating it very quickly, collecting all of the Glorbs, or destroying all of the slo-mo doodads
-Team Fortress Characters... But no hats or F2P model?
-The game's name shortens to STFU
Cons:
-The replay viewer is very limited. You can't save replays, and I feel as though you should be able to control the camera to watch the various prespectives rather than just following your "Main" prospective. Also, in the Helladeck, the replay stops at your very last glorb according to your main prespective, meaning your replay can be cut short of how long the actual playthrough was.
-It can be frustrating when trying to get a fast time on a level, because once you defeat the boss, you can't rewind time and do it faster. You have to time out your shifts just before the boss is defeated, or the level ends, and your time is a little longer than it should be. This also means you can't re-wind through the whole level to make sure you didn't miss anything.
I feel the pros definitely outweigh the cons, and like I said, this has worked its way up to one of my favorite games on steam.  If you have fifteen dollars on hand, I highly reccomend you buy STFU, or you had just better STFU.

For a first time player like me, this has been a really enjoyable experience. I never played the original release as I'm strictly a PC gamer, so I was able to come into this title with no expectations and a clear, level head.
---
The good stuff:
The story and cast of characters are engaging and really grabbed my attention. I didn't expect the story to go the way it did and every time I thought it was over, something else happened and it continued. Most of the characters had a decent amount of growth, except the main character. He basically stuck with his original personality throughout the entire game (not a complaint).
Game performance was consistent and enjoyable throughout my entire playthrough of the game, the true ending and the eX+ content. I held an extremely smooth and consistent 60fps the entire time with my system. 4790k/290x/16gb
Now for the bad stuff:
Until you get accustomed to the controls, the combat can feel a bit clunky. Somewhere between a fast paced version of Cold Steel and a slower clunkier version of Ys. Once you get used to it, it becomes much more enjoyable.
The story had a few slower moments, but they were few and far between.
Not enough time spent with Rion. Just sayin'.
---
The Verdict:
With this being a remaster/port of a 2 year old game, I honestly cannot justify the $60 price tag. It's an excellent game, but it's several years old at this point and honestly it deserves something more like a $40 MSRP because of this. If you're interested in the genre and/or Falcom games in general, go buy it. It's totally worth it.

If you're not new to Falcom games, this is the game that merges Trails of Cold Steel's generic+tropey+cliche yet good and fun story with Ys fast-paced action RPG combat.
If you're mew to Falcom games, they're a company whose niche is making mostly action jrpg's with predictable yet fun stories. And the games that are turn-based have such a huge emphasis in fleshing out their worlds that the only other comparison I can make is Witcher.
If you played the Vita version, prepare to be salty as this is the definite version of the game, and it brings:
1) Stable 60 FPS and higher resolution
2) New side stories (basically dungeons with a little plot to flesh out the character relationships)
3) After Story: A new chapter that takes place after the main story.
4) New playable characters at certain parts of the game.
5) Expanded friend pages
6) Battle changes - combat has been made a lot more difficult than the Vita version, like the addition of new EX Skills
7) New difficulty options - Calamity, higher than Nightmare, possibly rivaling Inferno mode from Ys games. Infinity mode is also an option for NG+ and can be paired with the existing difficulty settings. Wanna do Calamity + Infinity? :D
8) Kou can now decorate his room and this triggers more options.
Story-wise this is a tongue-in-cheek parody of Trails. Combat-wise this is in par with Ys VIII (which isn't out yet on Steam).

Tokyo Xanadu eX+ is the updated and upgraded version of the previously released vita game, Tokyo Xanadu, boasting improved HD graphics, additional story content - presented in the form of both post-chapter side stories and post-game content - as well as improved framerates.
As always with Falcom's games, one may or may not find the opening sequences to the game somewhat generic and lacking in many departments, Though that is - in my opinion - what makes their games so intriguing and special. Falcom has a way of taking generic settings, ideas, and sterotypes found in other mediums, and taking them that one step futher to create something genuinely stunning and unforgettable.
Tokyo Xanadu has an interesting premise no doubt, however that's not to say that the story is comparable to that of Falcom's flagship Trails series. Though interesting enough, the story boils down to (for the most part) episodic sequences that contain slice-of-life moments, an introduction or reveal that leads to the climax, the climax, and finally a wrap up of the chapter (pretty similar to Cold Steel 1). Though great in its own right, just don't expect anything quite
amazing.
Think Ys with slower paced combat. The Trails series, with near identical story and character progression. This game for the most part, follows the same three day story structure each chapter.
is your slice-of-life wandering around areas doing quests and whatever.
is the lead up or climax of the chapter, and
is the conclusion to the chapter.
Tokyo Xanadu, like Ys, takes an action combat approach to the game, and oh boy does it get fun. Once you get past the tutorial dungeons, you'll be speeding through corridors, slaying enemies left and right, switching out party members, all the while in pursuit of the dungeon's boss.
I am blown away by the amount of detail Falcom have put into their world. From the bookstores and hardware stores in Station Street, to the Arcades and Florist in the entertainment district and Brick Alley respectively. If you have played through any of Falcom's previous titles you
no doubt find amusing and downright in-your-face references left and right. This also includes bonding scenes!
Graphic wise, there's not much to coment on. It's pretty good for a HD remaster and quite the bit better than Cold Steel I and II, while falling behind CSIII. It might not blow anyone's mind, but at least the expressions are there, and there are some pretty impressive character models.
This time around, Aksys teamed up with Ghostlight to create the port. I can safely say that this game runs like a dream on my i3 6100 GTX 1060 3GB at 1080p and yes, that is overkill. I have seen reports of this game running on 5 year old laptops with minimal frame drops @60fps.
Translation wise, Aksys have taken it upon themselves to look over the script from the Vita version and for the most part, I have had absolutely no complaints about the translation quality. With the help of the beta testers, most if not all grammar and text errors should have been ironed out. I wouldn't say that it is to the standards we've all come to expect out of  XSEED, but nothing I have come across so far has taken away from my enjoyment.
- The enemy targeting system can feel - at times - clunky, preventing you from locking onto your desired target.
- Dungeon design. Though each main dungeon has its own defining aesthetic, the designs are straightforward, with the occasional branching corridor.
- The button combos to do certain actions can be a bit too sensitive(?). For example, when trying to air dash across gaps, you may end up charging up an aerial spin attack with Kou.
- The linear story progression may start to show its wear. Going back to square one and etc..

Freedom Planet may look like a Sonic knockoff to you, but it's not. Freedom Planet is a 2D Fast-Paced Beatemup game made by Indie Group, Galaxy Trail, where game design is amazing, the characters are well-drawn and look great, there's some gimmicks that will bring back memories, and an amazing soundtrack. You get to play as Sash Lilac the Dragon Girl (fast and a wide variety of moves to use) Carol Tea the Wildcat (uses a motorbike to fight and can walljump) and Milla Basset the Hound (able to dig some spots to find items), running at speed of sound and fighting against an insurmountable amount of enemies and obstacles that will stand in your way.
This is a speed/combat-based game that has alot of nostalgia within it for those who played Sonic, Ristar and/or Gunstar Heroes. I have repeated some stages that I like, not because of the soundtrack, but mainly because of the bosses. The features involve Adventure Mode (For those that love cutscenes and prefer to have an in-depth look into the whole story), Classic Mode (For those that just want to get into the action and are not concerned about the story), and Time Attack (For those looking to break personal records and reach the top of the Leaderboards). Character designs look great, there was talk about the first character designs, but I like the current ones right now,

Do you like classic Sonic games? If the answer is yes, then this game is for you. If the answer is no, well, I'd still say give it a shot anyway.
I was looking forward to this game as soon as I looked at it on Steam Greenlight, I love Sonic 2 and this game is clearly heavily inspired by the Sonic games on the Genesis. Though I do think this game isn't as much about speed as Sonic the Hedgehog is. There are plenty of times where you'll be doing less running and more puzzle solving, combat or platforming.
The keyboard controls are fine as far as I can tell, and they can be customized to your liking. If you think a game like this should be played with a controller, then there's that option too.
Graphically speaking, the game has gorgeously done spritework with really expressive characters and fantastic animations, the environments are really nice too. And with better processing available, even more impressive stuff can be done with the sprites and could ever be done if this were a Genesis game. The music is also quite good and really reflects the world you're travelling through.
There are some negatives which I'll list quickly:
1. Some stages feel like they go on for a few minutes longer than they should, mainly on the first playthrough.
2. There are some times where it's virtually impossible not to take damage from an enemy attack, luckily you have a pretty substantial life bar and healing items are fairly abundant.
3. I'm not a fan of limited lives, but getting extra ones is pretty easy since you only need 200 gems for an extra life, and gems are really easy to get a lot of.
4. The story can be kind of annoying to skip through if you stop playing in the middle of a stage and come back, though you can skip them and there is an option to play the game without the story.
Other than those nitpicks, this game is really good, and I have no regrets purchasing it.

I didn't expect much out of this for a mere five bucks, but this baby has layers. And new ideas. And polish. It is clear that every little detail was intentional...
Alright, so there is an overworld 'hub' where you have some interesting things to manage. You populate the hub with characters you find in the dungeon (
). The currency is points that you get from combos, and later, followers. Some of the characters you unlock are 'followers' that generate points just like an idle clicker game.
Okay, so you have these points and you spend them in the overworld on loadout options.
The core combat game has a heavy deck building theme going on. It's neat. You can keep any given card and reap the buff, OR you can burn it to get health. Really neat risk/reward thang. You find the cards in chests, but opening them will cost you some health (it shows you how much before hand). Some cards are 'bones', and you take them to the hub... And craft dudes.
You can leave the dungeon by jumping out of a window. This takes you back to the hub world to save cards for future runs, spend points, get full health, and restart the dungeon (new random layout). So really, you can 'grind' your way to a more powerful state if you play it safe and leave a few times. Brilliant.
. There is a metric ton of new ideas in here, and I can't go over them all BUT if you are interested, I highly recommend reading this guide here (the game is super obscure, so

First off, this game is beautiful. I can honestly say that the graphics have bested any game that I have played to date, but as most people know, it's not the graphics that make the game, but the gameplay.
The story in this game is, in my eyes, touching. You won't find any crazy plot twists in the game, but the narrative viewpoint of a Father telling his daughter a story is wonderful, and while it has been done many times before, I feel like this game has done it in a unique and artistic way that adds depth and character to the game. Many will disagree, but I for one got completely engaged in the story from start to finish.
The gameplay in this game is good, not great, but good. The grappling hook type device you have combined with rocket boots and a superjump make this game really enjoyable in both a casual and competetive way. For example, you can just sit back and watch as you float effortlessly across skies filled with stars, or go completely hardcore and speedrun the game. On the other hand, the gameplay can get a little repetetive further along in the game, but it was the scrutinizingly detailed landscapes and immersive story that kept me coming back. I feel like this is more of a piece of art than a game, which in my opinion is a good thing, and I did purchase it in the summer sale, but I would pay full price for it any day. 8.5/10.

Mafia II is a story-driven FPS which is, ultimately, rather satisfying.  That said, there are a number of negatives: the story is very linear, with almost no scope for deviating from the current objective; too much of the in-game time is taken up with simply driving from place to place in the city; you have no choice in your response to events, which prevents you the player from ever becoming fully invested in Vito and his life, and the ending is... well, rather abrupt.
On the plus side, the graphics are atmospheric, the visual differences between time spent in the 1940s (in the early part of the game) and 1951 are clear and interesting, and the in-car radio system generates a good playlist of appropriate music.  Although I am not at all convinced that some of the 50s tunes were around in 1951 - in fact, I am pretty sure that the Everly Brothers hit "Dream" was much, much later.
If you want a simple shooter interspersed with cutscenes explaining why you are about to do whatever the next task may be, then this fits.  I enjoyed the game, despite my criticisms, and would recommend it to players looking for something which doesn't require too much thinking.

Usually I am in the business of reading reviews instead of writing them, but today I make an exception because this game is just not a good game.
I bought both COH1 and COH2 during the Summer sale.  I could not care less about multiplayer, as I am more into campaigns when it comes to RTS games.  COH delivered a cohesive and fun campaign that I enjoyed, and I probably put over 40 hours into it.  I particularily liked the artistic delivery and the campaign storyline, which was done in a very simplistic manner while also trying to give the gamer scenarios that were somewhat based on historical events.  COH1 was also very campaign-oriented, with all of the campaigns listed straight up in the main menu.  Options were easily accessible too.
When I finished COH1, I jumped right into COH2.  I had assumed that this would be a better game since it was made several years later, and the campaign appeared to fixate on the Soviets that time.  And we all know by now that it is very hard to screw up an RTS game with Soviets as a faction.  But man, right from the main menu this game looks like hot trash.  Even though I have this on the proper resolution, I can barely even read the text.  Most of the crap right in the main menu has to do with promoting multiplayer (aka DLC-fest) such as Twitch streams and other unwanted crap.  Even though my PC is past all of the recommended requirements, I couldn't get FPS past 50FPS even with tweaking all options to low values (made no difference if they were high or low, still wasn't getting 60FPS).
Then I tried the campaign.  First mission: retaking Stalingrad.  It looked familar.  Why?  Because I had happed to have just replayed the original Call of Duty a few days ago, and this mission was IDENTICAL to the CoD Stalingrad mission.  This all really explains the purpose of COH2: to capitalize on unoriginal concepts (like with all of the Soviet paraphenalia in the main menu, treating the hammer and sickle like a brand label).  The other thing that really jumped at me was the whole CGI story element; completely overdone and unnecessary compared to how COH1 handled its plot.  This story element is quite intrusive, especially with the new version of the tactical maps that they force you to endure throughout a mission: instead of a useful map like in COH1, you are now forced to view some completely useless black and white photograph.  What is the point?  There is no point.  And overall, the story just sucks.  It feels like a rehash of how World in Conflict handled its plot, except that WiC was based on a fictional WW3 scenario and COH2 is supposed to be based on non-fiction WW2.  So why change the direction now after COH1 nailed it beautifully?  It's like watching the difference in movies between classic horror special FX and CGI greenscreen crap.
And here's the best part: I'm only on the second mission.  I've spent a few hours trying to beat it, but I cannot.  It should be simple enough, but the game refuses to let me finish it.  I think it's a terrible mission design, especially when you have to burn some buildings down with flamethrowers (but why only some buildings?  WTF is the point of this objective) with infinite waves of Nazis bumrushing you engineers.  I actually finished this mission yesterday without too many problems, and then the game crashed of course.  Now, I am unable to even progress through the mission because every time I am supposed to use the engineers to blow stuff up, they are already dead before I can even control them!
And I honestly don't even know if I want to continue with this BS.  The game just looks and feels like crap compared to COH1.  Even the text, and the in-game UI itself, just looks terrible.  Everything is just so limp-dicked compared to how COH1 handled things.  So I think I'm going to check out some mods for COH1 instead.

LISA the Painful is a 2D scroller that also has turn based combat very similar to games such as Earthbound. The gameplay is one of the best I’ve seen for a RPG since unlike most RPGs there is no need to grind for XP and magazines (the currency in LISA), which makes progressing feel a lot more natural and entertaining.  The combat while basic, it is very unique in the sense where many character including your main character have a combo system. In this combo system when you do an attack you can insert a combo, and depending on your combo you will hit an enemy but also do a certain ability depending on the combo. As someone who is usually not a fan of turn based RPGs, this game really made me enjoy its combat system.  You might think that the game has painful in the title to sound edgy or cool, but it is actually a painful game. Party members you receive can permanently die, get kidnapped, or even abandon you. In the game you have to make very tough choices that will make you question your morality and your survival. Your main character also has an addiction to a drug called joy, which if you don’t give in and constantly take it he will receive a joy withdrawal and not be able to do many of his combo attacks. Also supplies in the world are very scarce and the world is honestly a hell-hole, and the game certainly does a great job at immersion.
The main thing this game has going for me is the story. This story is one of the greatest stories in a video game I have ever seen. I do not want to spoil too much, but the basic summary is that your character Brad Armstrong finds a baby which turns out to be a girl, in a world where woman no longer exist. Brad decides to take care of the baby and raise it with his good friends. A few years pass and when the girl is no longer a baby and a child, she is kidnapped. It is now Brad’s job to find his daughter, and face whatever stands in his way. The game is a train wreck of sadness, but there are also many humorous bits in it. The story has so much detail similar to the Hotline Miami series, and there are many twists and turns that await you within the story. I think it will definitely move you.
The last thing I want to talk about is the music. This game’s OST is amazing as it is very unique and while it seems odd, fits the world of LISA perfectly. The sound effects within the game are also very appealing and well done, and in my opinion sound design is something very important that this game succeeds in.
I highly recommend LISA the Painful, and if you like this game you should also get LISA the Joyful, which is the dlc that concludes the game. You might also want to try out LISA The First since it’s free, but it is very different from The Painful and The Joyful. Overall, I think this game is a hidden-gem that is a must get.

Company of Heroes 2 is a welcome return to a forgotten form of RTS for many. The games core mechanics and systems are easy to grasp, but new players will quickly find themselves overwhelmed by the pace and brutality of the combat. In many ways, that's okay - seven years waiting for the series to return proper and Relic know how to appease its fans, that much is certain. At the end of it all, Company of Heroes 2 is the whole package. If you PC can handle it, expect a beautifully bloody trip through one of the most horrific times in history. From its thundering sound design to the intricatley polished RTS mechanics, this is another unmissable release from Relic Entertainment.

Greetings my fellow commanders!
Company of Heroes 2 (CoH 2) is a worthy successor to the first Company of Heroes game. I am particularly glad that CoH 2 is better in allowing players to focus more on the tactical and strategic aspects of gameplay rather than getting bogged down on micro-related tasks e.g. reversing a vehicle. With the introduction of the Soviet Union, the Axis forces now face an additional foe, making the battlefield more deadly and more interesting.
Instead of three doctrines per faction as in CoH 1, each faction gets a diverse set of commanders to tailor gamers' tactical tastes and strategic approach. These are highly commendable features and one should not view them as simple cash-grab corporate strategies. After all, Relic is also a company that needs money to make more high-quality games for us gamers, provided that they DO remain faithful to us.
CoH 2 supports Steam Workshop but I wish that Relic would allow gamers more freedom with regards to Decals and Skins (as long as they are historically accurate). For instance, if you want to take the role of the 1st SS Panzer Division LSSAH, you may wish to attach the division's insignia onto your vehicles but such an option is not possible for ranked multiplayer matches. I am guessing these would be simple updates and I hope Relic reads this review to implement these features.
I am particularly glad that the community for this game is very much active in the forums and on social media channels like Twitch and YouTube. With such a wealth of community contribution, I believe this game has a bright future. Let us hope that Relic continues to invest more resources into developing this great game and incorporate more high quality features into future versions of the CoH franchise.
Hope to see you on the battlefield!

Maybe not quite as good as the Dragonfall campaign but Hong Kong is still a great cyberpunk RPG within an awesome, unique setting full of detail.
Would recommend playing through Dragonfall first and if you like that getting onto HK is a no-brainer.

The last addition to the new SR incarnation. Hacking got revised, the characters are as interesting as they were in Dragonfall. Overall Harebrained continue to deliver on the level they did Dragonfall. Consequences for your actions counting towards the choice of endings is a very nice touch. Also some nice easter eggs for you to find.
- Bonus campaign is a (somewhat) discouragement. Aside from the "no good ending" thing (which can be expected in cyberpunk setting), there are no middle-ground choices - and this diminishes your decisions somewhat if you got to know and care about your team.
- In several missions the anount of enemies coming in waves is excessive, they are effectively trying to throw cannon fodder at you and hope you'll run out of bullets (or medkits). Not the best way to provide difficulty.
- A nasty bug of "freezing" in the middle of enemy turn. Gets especially annoying in said "long battles". The only two options are to
a) replay the battle from earlier saves - save often!
b) Try to Alt+F1, then CMD > ENDTURN [Enter] for forced end of turn. Often leads to problems on its own, use with caution.
All and all, if you liked Dragonfall you'll probably like Hong Kong as well.

The story was great in my opinion, most the characters were pretty likeable and had interesting backstories. Gaichu and Gobbet being my two favorite companions. Apart from your companions, a lot of the vendor NPC's have pretty cool stories as well and they progress as you talk to them. The game did feel a bit short for an RPG, but then again I can't say I didn't enjoy every minute of it. On a final note there are noticable bugs still in the game, however they never became too distracting in my playthrough, so it didn't matter too much to me. Overall I would definitely recommend this game, I had a ton of fun.

just 4 hours in, and Ive run into two rather annoying bugs... The first, resulting in failure of an optional ojbective on the main queswt in "City of Darkness".. The second, is inside the Matrix.. So many dead spots where you need to click, and sadly, this time its like playing frogger, but you cant get spotted by the multiple protection codes inside.. It can cause you to just stand there, and get spotted, or run somewhere you had NO intention of moving, resulting in being spotted.. VERY annoying!!
It also seems extremely dumbed down from previous versions, which I enjoyed thoroughly.. I havent yet decided on Honk Kong or not..
The Matrix has been overhauled, and I haver to say, I prefer the old way.. I like the actual 'hacking' part of it, but moving around, feels like playing frogger..Idk.. While im inside of it, I dont get a joyful feeling.. More like "i just want to get it done, and get back to the game"..
Flanking, and Cover is just broken.. But I believe its been this way in all 3 titles Ive played.. Not counting forcing a character out of cover, there are often times where you are in cover, enemies are ONLY in front, and are still being gien flanked bonuses!  It is extremely annoying, and I have to wonder why they bother implementing th system, and how its managed to STILL be an issue after this long?! Shaman (the class I chose for my first HK run) was a bit underwhelming.. I chose to play as a pure summoner, and found out that there are a VERY limited number of summons.. With your fetishes costing over 1,000Nuyen, and Nuyen being very tight this time around, youre forced to go without fetishes (or only rank 1&2 which are glorified meat shields) or go without spells, armor, etc.. I dont even think there is a Summon point in each mission.. Those that do, have only a single one!  I believe there was ONE mission that had two, but I could be mistaken, and it was only the one.. And they do NOT last long! 2 turns, maybe 3, unlike your fetishes, that can last longer depending on your control.. They make great support roles however, but playing summons was a complete waste of a player character, and Im extremely disappointed by it! Even with a high Summon control, and investment into Charisma (I have 11 Charisma, 9 spell cast, 7, and 6 in the Charisma tree) Summoned creatures are weak as♥♥♥♥♥♥. Attacks do minimal damage, and the spell options are pretty bad (admitedly, I did NOT once use a rank 5 fetish)..I also had issue with the Ley Lines spell.. At first, it worked as intende.. Allowed my Acid attack to bounce up to three targets, making it useful.. By the time I began using Acid Surge 3, and then 4, it was no longer bouncing to targets (for the last SEVERAL missions!)
The story, is still very well done, and while it may not be your favorite, its still well written, and does an exquisite job of painting that mental picture, and really bringing you into the scene completel.. Conversations are very well done, but the characetrs are so spread out in this ridiculous town, that it gets to be a real chore running to everyone to talk after each mission(ending a mission triggers new conversation options with npcs)..
Equipping allies with arms/armor can be a real PAIn in the behind, and with the lack of Nuyen, isnt really something one would want to do.. But still, its nice to give your heavy hitters the most powerful weapons, and armor... I wa sconstantly broke, and never once purchased a consumable.. Cant imagine If I would have needed to buy those also.. Final mission, and I have 2Nuyen... Literally!

Let me start of by saying that Platformer is one of my favorite genre.
Making a good platformer is hard, you need good controls, good level/enemy/boss design and a decent challenge.
Many indie developers tried to make retro style platforming games over the years thinking it MUST be easy to make a good platformers, you just need sprites, a few bosses and maybe a few gimmicks here and there, this resulted in a lot of mediocre, uninspired platformers.
I can safely say that this game is not one of those, this game got it right.
I've seen a lot of people saying that this is just a Sonic clone but this is absolutely wrong, this game is inspired by classics such as Sonic, Megaman and Ristar while still adding a lot of its own style, the game still have it's own identity.
In term of level design this is one of the best platformer i've seen in a long, long time, there is a multitude of paths you can take to get to you where you need to go and each paths almost feel like a new stage.
The game also control like a charm, it does not feel floaty and the 3 available characters all have distinct gameplay and movesets. (And exclusive stages!)
The challenge was also there, the stages difficulty felt just right and the bosses are all well designed and have some difficult patterns.
Freedom Planet is also very well presented, the music is great and the graphics are very nostalgic, the animations are great and fun to watch.
I was also strangely interested in the story between the stages, thanks to the good voice acting and funny characters. (You can skip the stories in classic mode if you want but seriously, it's fun to watch.)
Overall i was really suprised to enjoy this game, since i never liked sonic mainly because of it's terrible level and boss designs.
But then again, this is NOT a sonic clone.

By the law of averages, at least ONE spiritual successor to Sonic the Hedgehog's earlier games had to be good. Freedom Planet is this, and so much more. It's like the best Genesis Sonic games had a baby with Gunstar Heroes, and it grew up to be a Sega Saturn game. You have three characters that go through the same levels, but different paths thanks to their special abilities, amazing 32-bit chiptune music, level design that's as fun to look at as it is to play through, and crazy boss fights that are ungodly satisfying when you beat them.
While most fake-retro games try to ape the NES, Atari, or early PC games, Freedom Planet chooses the Sega Saturn as its inspiration, and it shows in everything from the color palettes and sound to the gameplay and UI. If I didn't know better, I'd say this WAS a Saturn game.
The only downside is that if you're sick of brightly-colored anthropmorphic animals on adventures with cosmic implications from exposure to Sonic fancharacters, the cast of Freedom Planet will do nothing to endear you to themselves. Luckily, GalaxyTrail thought of that. When you begin the game, you can choose to turn off all cutscenes and dialogue, playing it as if there were no story at all!
This fills the horrible void in my stomach left by Sonic.

I'll start with the gameplay; The game is really fun, and is a callback to the classic Sonic games. The characters are fun to play as, the level design is excellent and the bosses are really exciting (except for that stupid dragon). If you're in it for the gameplay, I definitely recommend this game. However, I have one gripe with the gameplay. The traction is insane. You can walk up walls or jump into a slanted ceiling and start running up. If the traction was a bit more sane, the gameplay would have no flaws at all.
Now on to non-gameplay related stuff. The music is really great, I love it. However, the voices were really grating. I hated them. Another thing I hate is the story. Normally, I wouldn't talk about the story on a Sonic-style platformer, but they clearly went out of their way for it, with a fully voiced story mode full of cutscenes (thankfully completely skippable by playing Classic mode). The characters are pretty awful, and I don't care much for their designs. Their personalities is where it really hurts though, as they're all pretty boring and annoying. If the cast was more interesting, perhaps I could have been more invested in the story. Also, the cutscenes are absurdly long for this kind of game. They should be much more concise and short. As I said earlier, the voiceacting really annoyed me, so that didn't help.
This next problem is a bit more important I think; The game can't seem to decide if that one city is using a Chinese or Japanese setting. It's an unholy mix of both, and it was really annoying me. Choose one and stick with it, make different places for both, or just make something new.
All in all, I recommend it, but only if you're in it for semi-solid Sonic-like gameplay and nothing else.

As a time-travelling super soldier, I'm glad that my primitive, barely-evolved ancestors can finally get a taste of life in the future.
Getting one-shotted by some jerk with pinpoint accuracy and panther-like reactions need no longer mean the end of your life when you can roll back time and summon another gun-toting Forcer to exact revenge on the aforementioned jerk and continue to blast through the levels.
If you have ever been a fan of side-scrolling shooters like Contra and Midnight Resistance, this game will be perfect for you. The sheer satisfaction of watching 30-odd versions of yourself complete a mission (a la Super Meat Boy), smashing and exploding the living heck out of everything is brilliant.
The time-travel mechanic introduces subtle puzzle-like elements into the mayhem, and by picking the right soldier for the right job can shave precious seconds off the clock, especially if you are a completionist like me and need to beat the tough Watcher challenges.
Each level is perfectly designed for a quick 5-minute blast and the boss fights are extremely gratifying. Although the campaign is only a few hours long if you rush through, the medals and challenges in each stage add more replay value on top of the more cerebral Helladeck content.
Overall, a great price for one of the most entertaining games of the year.

The platforming is good, although it suffers a little from being first person (as it makes it harder to sometimes know if you'll hit a boulder or just glide by it). At the same time, it's a bit unforgiving, some jumps you miss because you jumped slightly too early and you see the next platform just pass at arm’s reach, which is frustrating. The powered running jump can be tricky sometimes, as being first person you will sometimes run out of ground beneath you before jumping, resulting in you plummeting to death. I believe the game would benefit from a different respawn mechanic, as right now it kind of breaks the ambient just falling with a frog on your back silently judging her life options. Something like a last-ditch safety measure of the suit that would automatically make the jump to the previous platform, activated by the checkpoints (which could be beacons for that mechanism or simply tethering points for a rope). In terms of exploration it could also benefit from such a beacon system and a map - in levels where you want to explore you could fast travel between those beacons, for instance. It also needs some 'unstucking' mechanic, as right now you can become imprisoned between some rocks and buildings in one of the floating villages where you are unable to jump and stuck between some ice platforms, eternally falling. All in all, the story is not the strongest point, probably by the bleakness of the places you visit. There’s little lore to the world, few characters even acknowledge your presence in a world where you are a complete alien. It’s like a Martian coming down to earth in power armour jumping around all over the place and everyone just keeps on with their lives and ignore him, it breaks the illusion. There are a couple of youtube links right in the beginning that could be used to further explore the world (like video logs from his uncle providing tutorial info or his findings) but are simply links to jokes. It would be fun if some of those where given in the strange alphabet you find latter on, maybe giving clues to what happened to the frog people and your uncle. It seems it was well made in terms of programming the mechanics but felt short in story and world building.

Tropico 3 is a surprisingly good city builder or rather a 3rd world simulator. It is very different than games like Sim City and Cities XL. Those two games are more macro city builders, where in two or three mouse clicks you can make city blocks where 1,000 people might live. With Tropico and the Tropico series in general, you need to place each building, each road and your island along with the time it takes your construction company to build it. Your entire island might get to be 200 - 500 'Tropicans.'
Each Tropican has needs... Food, religion, job, healthcare, entertainment, safety and so on. The catch is every Tropican's needs have a certain weight to them based on what political party / faction they believe in. Each faction has major and minor demands. The military will want more soldiers, so you need to build an army base. The religious faction will want a church or cathedral. The capitalist party will want privatization or upscale entertainment. The communist party will want you to enable the free public housing edict or have adequate healthcare.
On top of that, you balance political relations with the USA and USSR. If they get too bad, one of the two will basically take over your country and it will be game over. It is interesting how many ways that you can get game over. The most common way to get a game over is to lose an election. You don't have to have elections even. You're in charge. If you don't want an election, the nationalist party will hate you and your loyalist party will love you. If you opt to have elections, it will be vise versca. People will call for early elections and when you have elections, you can see preliminary results and you can even sway (cheat) elections. Its all at the risk of a party's love.
It is pretty cool having to pick 3 things to make a speech about and then fulfill campaign promises, but its all pretty easy. Winning elections is pretty easy, especially compared to how difficult it was to win any elections in the original Tropico. It was so bad in that game, that it was almost impossible to win an election without stuffing the ballot box.
When citizens hate you, and there will be plenty that do, they will either peacefully protest or become rebels. Once you have enough rebels against you, they will attack your most remote buildings. Your army will then go fight them, but if the rebels outnumber your army, the rebel will win and the buildings will be destroyed. The rebels can attack your palace or flat out assassinate you for a game over.
Tropico has a single player campaign with a lot of scenarios. You don't just pick scenarios, you unlock them. Each scenario seems to have scenario specific events that only occur in the scenarios. Some scenarios last 30 minutes, others a few hours as you take an island from 1950 - 1990 or so. At the start of each scenario you can pick a player character from historical tropican dictators or make your own avatar. You can even make personality traits that will result in pros and cons. It can drastically change your play style if you are incorruptible and never have any crime or have a green thumb and have high farm yields at the cost of low factory production.
Your businesses, mines, farms, and everything requires citizens in them to function and make you money. Every citizen has different education levels that will impact who does what. So you need to build high schools and colleges. Once built, there are options to gear students to military or religion. You can also click vacant positions to hire foreign experts for a price. If you have more businesses than citizens, build an immigration office and let anyone into the country or change it to only let in skilled workers so you keep bums out of your country.
Nothing is done automatically. You place a building, then wait for your teamsters and construction crews to build it. The more crews and personnel you have working, the faster it'll get done. I'm happy with that. Its part of the realism. If there's a building you want developed faster, you can increase or decrease its priority. If its still taking too long, just have your avatar stand next to the building to get it done faster.
The graphics are beautiful and you'll see every Tropican walking around, hopping in their car and driving to locations. The music is nice and very Tropican / Salsa music. The radio DJ and the rebel DJ will provide a lot of flavor to what you're doing. The rebel DJ will always heckle you and every line is said with tongue in cheek humor. The game knows you're all powerful and while being a dictator is usually seen as a horrifyingly negative thing, the humor twists it into a silly positive thing.
The only letdown is the fact there are no Steam achievements, yet it is the Steam Special Edition.

Video review:
Shadowrun Hong Kong is a great way to start off your Shadowrun experience, but not a great way to end it. If you’ve never played a Shadowrun game before and you’re interested? If you like turn based strategy? Love reading in-depth stories? If Shadowrun lore is something you can get behind? Get this game. Don’t hold back. Have fun. But if you’ve played Shadowrun Returns and Shadowrun Dragonfall? You’re in for a HUGE disappointment. Allow me to tell you why.
First off for those that don’t know what Shadowrun is. Shadowrun Hong Kong is an isometric turn based strategy game where you organize a team of mercenaries known as shadowrunners, equip yourself with gear, and complete your missions in any number of ways whether that be by going in guns blazing or finding a way to use your skills with people or technology or what have you to get around the threat. And then of course there are some forced sequences as are necessary to push a narrative. It’s the third title in the series and the big ♥♥♥♥up here is that nothing has really improved since the previous title, Dragonfall, which was a standalone expansion at that.
The story is very bland and the characters are the most unrelatable, unlikeable, and uninspired characters that I have seen all year. Their reasons for coming together make literally no sense and their backstories are the most uninteresting thing that I have ever read for 60 minutes straight in my entire life. This edition of Shadowrun comes jam packed with extra writing. Too much writing. Seriously. The complete lack of voice acting in the text after three games now plus the huge increase in writing that is done makes playing Hong Kong feel like you’re reading a book. It’s like they heard that Dragonfall had too much forced fighting so they thought that fixing that meant forcing reading and only reading on us in every instance where there used to be fighting. They took one broken yet tolerable concept and did a 180 spin and broke it to a point where following the story is such a bore because you have to read a novel before you can even do a single mission.
The gameplay is a little harder than the previous shadowrun titles which is good considering how easy those ones were. The downside is that there isn’t actually much gameplay due to all the reading that you have to do. They did sort of make new skills and split other skills up as a way to force you to have to use more karma and thus be weaker as well. Like, now you have to upgrade a cyberware skill which needs your body skill raised along with it on top of having to be able to find and afford cyberware. Means that now if you want the best cyberware you’ll be spending fifty or more karma just to do that, and Shadowrun Hong Kong doesn’t give you more karma to compensate for this either. The gains are still the same. The routine of the game is still getting to the safe zone, talking to everyone, going on a mission, coming back, talk to everyone again, repeat. All the added reading means you’ll be spending twice as long running around the open home area as you will be spending on missions; just reading things.
The animations have changed for the better in battle and for the worse when you run around. Now your character running around looks like a flamboyant drunk attempting to get somewhere fast. The graphics and sound effects have seen zero improvement since Shadowrun Returns. The whole game just felt like a test to see how much they could get out of the same engine and resources before they had to spend money on something new. The menus and interfaces are mostly intact, but some have been changed. The ones have been changed include the karma screen which dumped the easy to navigate scroll screen and exchanged it for a different menu for every single stat. That makes for extra work to navigate your menus as a result.
Overall, Shadowrun Hong Kong is milk. That’s what it is. It’s Harebrained Schemes trying to milk one last chunk of money out of what they’ve done for two games already. Those that love shadowrun and haven’t played the previous games? They’ll love this! Those that have played the previous ones and actually enjoy seeing progress and upgrades in a sequel will hate this. I’m actually really sad to see that this is how they chose to end such a great series. With minimal effort and a bunch of regressive “fixes”. Shadowrun Hong Kong gets a 3/10 from me.

I'm not going to lie I'm surprised I didn't come across this game sooner.
First off before I ramble about the game I'll flat out say (for anyone here who is genesis lingual) this game I was almost convinced was made by the Sonic team. It was almost like an orgy of old gen sonic, ristar, gunstar heroes and vectorman had a four-way baby. So I may make a lot of references towards those games because this one brought back a LOT of nostalgia for me.
Anyway the game is you playing either Lilac or Carol (and there's another character named Milla but she's only played in classic mode). The story starts off that an alien dictator Brevon (who reminds me of Zinyak from Saints Row IV a little) coming to the planet to kill a king and brainwash his son into doing what he wants (I don't know why he probably could have just invaded but whatever) and [MEANWHILE] Lilac and Carol see a spaceship falling on the planet where they meed Torque whose an alien (but dresses as a duck to not scare locals).
Anyway it turns into a big debocal where they have to get several emporers, generals, mayors etc. to join to face Brevon. But in doing so each of the characters run into old aquaintences, trouble with the law, etc. So that being said I'll start off what I think of each component of the game.
STORY:
Okay surprisingly this game has a decent story. Some of the dialogue is something you've seen before but the characters are identifiable, they're cute and the sequences of the story aren't the stupid "THIS IS YOUR DESTINY" cliche, the characters will admit they're scared you'll ♥♥♥♥ up. It's definitly rated G as far as "if this were a movie" goes but there were several moments I was like "DAYAM♥♥♥♥♥♥THAT HAPPENED!" It does also have a Sonic the Hedgehog vibe to it but it's still a decent story. Whether you're a pupil or an adult the story of the game does grab your attention long enough to where I didn't find myself skipping most of the storyline, there was even a teary moment at the end (but you have to see what it is yourself I'm not spoiling it) (or go to youtube, cuz ♥♥♥♥ you). And if you don't care for the story, lucky you you can just skip it.
SOUND:
The game for being what reminds me of a Genesis/Super Nintendo funny enough does well with the sound effects, the voice acting (yea it's not just a beep in between dialogues) and music. For this game's genre type I give it an A.
CONTROLS: Being that it's only arrows and three buttons you gotta worry about the controls are very fluid and they're timed perfectly. There are several moments that require a combo in each level but they're easy to figure out. And you're going to need to know because quite frankly there are points where sometimes there's no enemies to a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. But you'll know what you're doing by then.
GAMEPLAY: Honestly it's fun as hell. It's fast paced (like sonic the hedgehog), there's explosions everywhere (like vectorman/sonic) the combos are fun to use, the bosses are hard as ♥♥♥♥ later in the game, like you literally have to start memorizing their fight pattern like a mother ♥♥♥♥er, and there's difficulties of Casual, Easy, Normal and Hard. I was on Normal, dear God some parts I didn't think I was but it didn't matter this game makes you want to keep going back. The character/enemy/boss varieties are fun and unique too.
REPLAY: I'm starting my second campaign with the other character right after the frustration of beating the final boss, I love this game.
OVERALL: I personally think this game is worth the try, whether you're thinking about picking it up for a steam sale or just looking for another side scroller to kill time I promise this one you'll find spending a whole day (like I did) beating it. It's also a good nostalgia for old school Genesis and Nintendo players. I like the soundtrack, the characters, the gameplay, everything about this game.
The only thing I'll say is I think would harm this game is some people may probably relate it too much to Sonic as if they pretty much ripped off the game, but I noticed in the credits at the end there was a special thanks to a particular Sonic Team (not THE sonic team) but it definitly shows the game was heavily influenced by it, and I believe Ristar, Vectorman and Gunstar Heroes as well. I love it when a game takes elements from others and just makes an awesome game.
I give this game an A.

Wow, I really can't recommend this game highly enough.  Freedom Planet may be a fairly shameless Sonic clone, but it's the kind of game we've all been wishing Sega would make for the last 20 years.  Since the end of the Genesis era Sonic games have suffered from a plethora of issues, from poor level design and bad physics to unnecessary padding and everything else in between, but Freedom Planet just nails it on every level.  The controls and physics are perfect, the level design is top notch with a ton of alternate paths through the game's enormous levels, there's multiple playable characters, hidden collectables to hunt for, and a ton of really awesome boss fights.  Oh, and besides all that, the game is also beautifully animated and has great music and voice work, and the story is surprisingly charming.  It's also really long for a game of this type and has free DLC planned.
I've probably played at least 500 platformers in my life, and I can safely say this is a very strong contender for top 10.  I just can't believe this kind of incredible quality and polish came out of a first-time developer.  Some people may say that indie games have a lot of good ideas but generally can't quite match the polish and scope of the classics, but this is not applicable here.  This game stands up well against absolutely any game you might wish to compare it to.
If you have ever enjoyed a platformer, especially the Genesis Sonic games, you really need to get this game right now.

A Sonic clone you ask? Nay I say, how can a clone be better than the original?
It's quite true that Freedom Planet plays a lot like the classic Genesis Sonic the Hedgehog games, particularly Sonic 2. The pace is fast, the levels are designed for quick maneuvering, you collect powerups to keep yourself alive, and there's multiple routes through every zone.
Everything about this game screams awesomeness, every bit of dialogue has very well done voice over, every cutscene has the charm of a Saturday Morning Cartoon. The story is compelling without being complex and reminds me a lot of Avatar The Last Airbender.
The gameplay control is super tight and feels great. Plug in a controller and go crazy, it's super responsive. Combat feels fluid and punchy and each of the three characters feels different enough to make additional playthroughs feel unique and fun.
The graphics are very retro without using that as an excuse to be lazy, everything looks gorgeous and the animations are all top notch.
Last, but not least, the soundtrack is incredible, and I don't know what else I can say beyond that.
If you're a fan of platformers, action cartoons, or old school Sonic the Hedgehog then you owe it to yourself to play this game, you won't be disappointed, I definitely wasn't!

After 26 hours of playtime, unlocking everything, collecting everything, and getting every achievement I think I'm finally ready to review Bit.Trip Runner 2: Future Legend of Rhythm Alien.
When I played this game for the first time, it evoked the same feelings I experienced playing games like Super Mario World, Crash Bandicoot, and Tetris for the first time. You sit there, not realizing that you're smiling and moving to the music and even humming along, and then it hits you; you're a kid again, and there's not a care in the world. It's almost magical. It's also everything a sequel could hope to be in every category, and it's become one of my favorite games on Steam. I could go on and on with statements like these (and they would all be true) but all you really need to know is if the game is fun or not, and the answer to that is absolutely, joyously, colorfully YES.
This game is not only a loveletter to fans of the original game (on which it improves on everything fans asked and hoped for and then some) but also to anyone who is a fan of stylish, musically driven platformers or rhythm games. The world is vibrant, hilarious and creative with giant, cartoonish backgrounds that will sometimes even distract you from the game with how funny and imaginative the situations are. This goes without saying but the music, a major boon and pivotal component of the gameplay, is completely stellar. Each world has a new song and you'll want to collect all of the music pickups as soon as you can to add more and more layers to the beat. The levels are laid out in such a way that each jump, kick, bounce and deflection adds a complementary tune to the soundtrack, and it makes you feel like the songs are not just background audio but a real part of the experience. The gameplay has been reworked and is far more about actual skill, timing and reflexes than the original Bit.Trip Runner's reliance on memorization and punishment through repetition. The moves are simple; you can duck, kick, jump, and block. Simple, right? It's the way Gaijin Games combines these basic manuevers in the levels that give you a real challenge that never feels cheap or frustrating so that when you lose, you know why and you're raring for another shot. You know how to duck and you know how to jump, but what happens when you're faced with a grounded and floating pair of enemies with space in between? You duck and jump at the same time, of course! A floating enemy with a wall underneath? You kick while sliding! In this way every new challenge feels organic and satisfying because you are mixing these moves that you've mastered to navigate these mazes of music that the developers have created for you. Soon you're flying through the air, blocking cubes, shattering floating enemies, jumping and sliding at a pace that will make onlookers think you must have been playing this game for years.
There's 5 worlds complete with bonus stages and hidden retro courses, unlockable characters and costumes, three difficulties (and optional checkpoints, THANK GOD), leaderboards, challenges and achievements, so you'll be playing this game for quite a while if you want to see everything it has to offer. At the price this game goes for now on sale, it's really a no brainer. Pick it up, pick up the soundtrack, maybe even grab a copy for your friend. Yes, it's that good. Happy running!

You've finally done it; you've invented time travel! But before you can begin to use it to make the world more better robots start falling from the sky, everything starts exploding, and a future version of yourself appears in front of you. Turns out time travel isn't quite all it's cracked up to be, but that's OK because the Super Time Force is here to fix all the stuff you screwed up and make the world more awesome for everyone! Though it's probably Capy I should thank, not the STF, for giving me some an awesome...time, with one of the most outrageously fun and intensely smart games I've played all year!
Super Time Force Ultra (the last word being as this is an updated version of the Xbox One/360 game) is a side scrolling shooter ala Contra, but with an insanely clever implementation of a time manipulation mechanic. The gist of this is you have the ability to rewind time at will, letting you back up and remedy a poorly done section or avoid a grisly death, all while your other character continues to run on their own timeline repeating your entire previous run before you rewound. What this means practically is you have the ability to stack characters on top of each other, allowing you to clear huge amounts of enemies, collect items, and quickly decimate bosses incredibly fast as dozens of versions of yourself run along the screen at once. Think the replay mode at the end of a Super Meat Boy level, except now everyone has guns.
But the mechanic doesn't stop as just a rewind button, but also allows you to save other versions of yourself by killing an enemy before they get to you, and then stacking your saved character onto yourself and doubling your firepower and lifespan. This not only lessens the blow of death, but actually makes it rewarding and almost encouraged, as well as completely destroying the frustration of a difficult segment or challenging enemy as it's so easy to rewind and do it again.
With so much rewinding and replaying segments it would be easy to have the pacing be absolutely sluggish and repetitive, but STFU accounts for this by giving you but 60 seconds to run through levels (though there are certain collectibles that extend this slightly) making it an all out dash for the end before time runs out. Frequently I'd find myself playing for hours without ever realizing it, as with everything moving so fast and absolutely no downtime it's ever so easy to melt away into the game and have it feel as if no time has passed at all.
I realize trying to take this all in makes STFU sounds like an immensely complex and stressful game, but the genius of it is that as soon as you get your hands on it everything is shockingly intuitive. Reading the "how to play" summary before starting the game had my head spinning, but within moments of playing the game everything fell into place and only continued to become more engaging and creative the longer I played and experimented with them. STFU is incredibly smart yet completely accessible to anyone that picks up the controller, and it's this fact that allows it to break out of the realm of just an interesting idea to being an insanely fun experience. It balances intelligent design with pure joy and entertainment with a deftness that is rarely achieved in any genre, no less one that has been floundering in a pool of uninspired mediocrity for the last several years.
But maybe ultimately what makes STFU so gratuitously delightful to play is the sheer amount of unrestrained fun you can feel emanating from every bit of the experience. From the gorgeously colorful art style, to the silly writing and even more ridiculous scenarios it's abundantly clear how much work developer Capy Games put into the game to make every single second as abundantly entertaining as it is. It's been far too long since I've played a game for the sole purpose of enjoying the hell out of it, and to be perfectly honest I cannot think of a single thing to complain about or that I feel could be improved upon in STFU. Capy has achieved excellence in all areas of design, and deserve a significant amount of commendation for what is almost certainly the most impressive game they've made in a long line of critical hits, and I can't thank them enough for finally bringing to PC.
In short I've had the
of my life, and can't wait to do it all over again (and I won't even need a time machine to do so)!

There's nothing quite like Super Time Force. Well okay sure some games can relate with the time travel rewind/fast forward mechanic, but it's in the way that STF handles player progression through levels that makes it the most genius time travel game ever.
So many moments, especially when going for better times and collectibles within a level, become struggles against not only well-thought-out enemy and hazard placement, but struggles against your own previous actions.
Are you .01 seconds away from getting the par time for a level? Rewind all the way to beginning to get the slow down shard that makes you appear faster in real time. Oh, you already got it? Find a way to shoot it offscreen before your previous self nabbed it.
Team member abilities and attacks are also ingeniously integrated into the main game and are (thankfully) utilized well in the Ultra edition's puzzle levels (the Helladeck). Shieldy is my favorite, as merely holding down with your shield charged allows you to bounce on and over enemies which has allowed me to breeze pass parts that were otherwise dead-ends in my speed runs.
New to this edition is the inclusion of "Ultra Force" characters which beyond toting a really neat black-and-purple color scheme and powered up attacks, aren't much more than a novelty. They do help in getting better times as they can do a bit more damage than the regular team however.
The graphics are crisp and charming, the animations even more so. STF never once slowed down for me, even when 30+ iterations of my characters were clogging the screen at once.
The only downsides to this package are the occasional menu crashes, the sometimes amatuerish-sounding and grating chiptune soundtrack, and a weird slowdown glitch that occasionally happens when you reload a level too quickly. And the story is cute but ultimately the humor is so cheesy-for-cheesy's-sake that it becomes painful, especially upon repeat playthroughs.
If you have this game already on XBLA I wouldn't recommend getting it again unless you A. Love it, B. Wanna support Capy Games, or C. Want more Super Time Force! I could definitely see these brilliant mechanics being expanded in new and interesting ways and if that were coupled with a story with a bit more weight and a bit less meme-humor (Think Shovel Knight), sequels to STF could be masterpiece-level gems.
Ultimately, Super Time Force (Ultra or not) is a smart and painstakingly designed videogame that oozes with the unique and distinct joy of the classic hazard-and-enemy laced platformer. Pick it up!

Before you consider playing LISA, you should know that it was created in RPG Maker, a Japanese rpg construction kit. This means that its gameplay mechanics are limited to what that engine can do, and that is pretty oldschool stuff: 2d side-scrolling world and turn-based combat.
Which makes the game all the more amazing for what it does - using very basic tools to tell a gut-wrenching story set in a charmingly decadent and degraded world; blatantly exploring dark themes spiced with hilariously awkward post-apocalyptic social situations; introducing a host of wacky characters, and posing truly messed up moral dilemmas. I would also argue that it has the most appropriate soundtrack ever created for a videogame.
So if you're into the whole Mad Max meets Naked Lunch meets SpongeBob SquarePants vibe, give it a go. Just remember not to wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle... That's lame as hell.
