Tl;dr It has simple gameplay with enough depth to appease hardcore strategy game enthusiast, great music, great dialogue, dark humor, and varied playthroughs for nice replayability. The story is unique and most if not all of the characters have some type of charm to them.
1. The Setting:
This game is just beautiful. The art is rather simple, but the writing helps get the point across and succeeds at every point in the game. You will be empathizing and feel happy and sad at the same time knowing that the problems in the game can reflect real life issues. I myself deal with drug addiction, so it sort of hits home a bit how taxing it can be on not only yourself, but those around you. Now to break it down, this game is essentially a sidescrolling dark-humored version of Earthbound set in a post-apocalyptic world where there are no more women aside from one young girl named Buddy, whose adoptive father is the man you play as throughout the entirety of the main game named Brad.
2. The Characters:
The game is based around having a party filled with random guys willing to fight for you, finding and trying to protect her from the dangers of a world filled with men who are bewildered and depressed due to the lack of women truly bringing the sense of dread throughout the entire game all while you see the growth and past of Brad dealing with his issues with drug addiction and neglect. Even Brad is somewhat of a danger to the person he cherishes most. Though, as depressing as the game can get, the game has great humor, and at some points, a certain type of cuteness some characters you meet will give you a sense of motivation to find out what will happen next. That goes without saying there are many wicked and utterly repulsive characters as well for those looking for a unsettling time.
3.The Exploration:
There are many paths you can go through for a bit of extra side story, but they are entirely optional. There is no real directive other than just explore everywhere that you possibly can, so it may be a bit confusing at some parts if all you want to do is complete the game. There is a good amount of decision making, and there are not decisions that have a small impact, so choose carefully and save often as the consequences are poignant. That said, some of your party members can die, get kidnapped, and abandon you. The is a lot of overworld items you can find if you exploit the environment, and find secret hiding holes with stashes of goodies in them. Be sure to search every nook and cranny of caves and be aware of cliffs with items on it if you don't want to miss out on anything. Sometimes you may have to take a painful fall to get to some areas.
4. The Difficulty:
As I mentioned before, you have a party of 4, essentially mercenaries(for a lack of a better word), including Brad who have different setups and playstyles to help synergize with one another. The gameplay is not too dependent on grining, though there are areas where you can, and the game paces the difficulty fairly. There is a pain mode which has exclusive enemies, makes the game harder statistically, and removes the ability to save multiple times at each save location. If you aren't one to be bothered by struggling through the game, you might want to save that for a different playthrough and just play the normal mode. Though, if you do, there is some things you can miss out on, because Pain mode has some areas and scenes locked to that mode only. If you want to get the full experience the first time through, you may want to play Pain mode, but if you want a relaxed non-stressful playthrough then stick with the normal mode. As a side note, the loading screens are very short as the game isn't graphically intensive, so you can save and experiment and just reload the game without worrying about being punished with wait times.
5. The Battle System:
There are many different effects and skills that characters can use, and even some bosses have perma-kill moves killing one of your characters outright who will be gone for good. Always be prepared when you see someone that looks a bit "off", and save before you think something major will happen. Some of them have multiple hits which have the chance to be a critical hit each time, or cause a status ailment, or heal your party members. Think of it as the typical Final Fantasy type rpg with a lot of elements from games like Earthbound. There is different equipment, weapons, and accessories you can get as well as miscellaneous items that are for characters who will only join you if you find their special item. Some characters, and a big one Brad, has Joy addiction and can suffer withdrawal symptoms lowering their stats for some time. You can rest or just wait it out, but they can be abated by taking Joy(the drug) which will give you a bit of a boost in battles as well as keeping the withdrawals away for a bit. Though, if you don't let Brad take Joy, you can still use your special attacks i.e Fireball attacks as they scale off your Special Attack stat which doesn't lower when you go through Withdrawals. So, you can avoid letting Brad take Joy through the entirety of the game, and just use the Joy on other Joy addicts to make them "Joyed" in battle, or sell it to prove that you don't need it. You might find that doing that pays off at some point in the game, or just as a personal accomplishment if that isn't good enough for you. There are other unique status effects like being drunk, weirded out, perpetually depressed, stinky, and scared all with their own drawbacks and benefits which you should look up on the wiki if you care enough. There's also the typical rpg status ailments like being poisoned, burned, paralyzed, and blinded. There are many shops throughout the game that you buy alcohol, which obviously makes you drunk, but also heals you, status healing items, equipment, and miscellaneous items that may recruit additional characters.
6. The Music and Sound:
By far my favorite thing in the game is the music. The music is simple but varied and catchy. There are so many areas where I just want to stand around and listen to the music, and some of the areas are quite grim and awkward to stand around in. There's such a wide variety of music and as someone with no real preference towards a specific genre, I am happy with all of the tracks. Some are eerie,, some sounds like club music, one is literally just grunting. If you're a music enthusiast and you also find buying soundtracks your thing, I would definitely decide on getting the complete edition of the game. The sound effects in the game also have their own charm and are very niche. It truly sounds like what an indie game would be like; very obscure unexpected sound effects that fit well and aren't annoying or repetitive.
Overall I would say this game is as close to a 10/10 as it can get. There are some small bugs and sometimes the game which may seem like it's wasting your time, though most of those parts are the optional areas which you can just bypass if you feel strongly enough about it. The problems with the game are so miniscule that you probably won't be making to much of a fit about it. Just remember to save often(unless you're in pain mode) and don't be surprised to not get it the first time. Some parts in the game may too subtle to get the first time or simply not present like what every stat does and the odds of hitting an ability, so be prepared to do a small bit of research if you wind up struggling with normal mode, or if you really want to get the most out of your characters and achieve a level of expertise at the game. Anyone I've seen in reviews have held this game in high esteem, and for good reason. This game is worth the value of $10, the DLC is worth getting if you're interested in the lore, and the Soundtrack is great if you're into the music and want to further support the devs.

All right, let's get something straight. This isn't a Sonic clone. It's more basically taking all the best action platformers on the Genesis, and putting it on one really, REALLY good game. There's bits of Sonic, sure. But there's also Ristar, Gunstar Heroes, Pulseman, Rocket Knight Adventures, Mega Man X... (Not technically a Genesis game, but you get my point)
You've got the general speed of the Sonic games, where you get a lot of chances to just go really fast and tear through things. When you get beyond that, though, there's some really good level design, with a good number of secrets and alternate paths. And there's some of the best boss fights I think I've ever played in an indie game for a long, long while, especially when you reach the later half of the game.  It's difficult enough you might need to use a couple of continues, but it's never unreasonable.
I've only beat the game with one character so far, and I'm probably going to get into another one soon. All the characters are really unique on their own, and some of them even get their own levels and bosses, which is a really nice touch. If you like action platformers at ALL, you really, really want this game.

This game is quite possibly one of the BEST indie game I've played.  Think Sonic, Klonoa, Vectorman, Megaman Zero, & whatever other great action platformer you can think of from days long past then throw them all in a Blender then what do you get?
FREEDOM PLANET
Great voice acting, humor inducing cut scenes, cute cuddly furry characters, solid action speed platforming, remarkable retro soundtrack, best boss battles I've ever seen in an old-school game & I've played a lot of old school games.
The game has Adventure mode, Classic Mode, & Time Attack.  Adventure is the main game, lots of story & such. The voice acting is top notch & sounds great.  Classic mode is the main game without the cut scenes, but these cut scenes are worth watching.  Time attack is pretty much what it sounds like.  Beat each level as fast as you can.
You can play as 2 starting characters & you unlock a 3rd character through the games Story Mode. Each character plays differently.
The main character Lilac is a Dragon Speedster who can attack with her hair like a whip & charge a dash in several directions.  While dashing she is immune to damage for about 1 second, but it takes a few seconds for it to recharge. She also has an aerial spin that gives her a slight hover double jump & also does damage but can be hard to control & hit with in certain situations so this move is best used on flying enemies.
The second, Carol, is a Feline that can jump up walls & relies on quick attacks which can take out enemies very fast. She also has a motorbike which you can use after finding gas tanks scattered throughout the levels.  This bike enables her to climb any wall & gives her increased mobility & a double jump that also deals damage. Carol is also the easiest to play out of the three characters available.
The third is Milla, a Puppy who has less health than the other 2 but can fly & charge to create blocks to then throw at enemies or use them to fire a beam & sheild herself from damage.  You have to unlock Milla by playing the first 2 levels in the Adventure mode & she's currently only available in Classic Mode after unlocking.  Milla will get her own Story Mode later on from what I've heard.
There are other characters that will be added later to the game as DLC.
The boss fights are fun & challenging.  If playing on the hard difficulty (or even on normal) you will have a rough time.  Every boss feels unique in how they attack you & has a strategy to figure out in order to beat them.  Some bosses have a chain attack & if you get caught in it you can expect nearly certain death.  During the tougher boss fights your friends will show up & throw health pickups your way or help deal damage to the boss with you.

The only negative thing I can say about this game is the FPS will randomly drop from it's normal 60 down to 30 at times & it will lock to 30 until you find a level transition.   This problem only occurs when running the game at higher resolutions or in 3x Size mode.  Also, the difficulty can get very frustrating at the later levels, but don't let that stop you from checking this game out.
In short, this is the epitome of what games were in the early 90's & anyone who wants a good old school platformer, action game shouldn't miss out on this one.

Shadowrun: Hong Kong is the cyperpunk RPG that fans of the genre have been wanting since the 90s when games likes Baldur's Gate, Arcanum, and many others dominated the RPG market.
With Shadowrun: Returns they made a decent base, but it felt bare bones and everything was a bit off, but with Hong Kong you feel like a Shadowrunner in a brutal, unique, dark, and intelligent cybperpunk world. You get to know each character of your party in detail, the citizens of your home city, and you get choices at every turn as to what kind of person you wish to portray. It is all very well done and unlike many other RPGs it even has a very satisfying ending.
The extended edition adds an extra campaign to tie up some loose ends that follows perfectly off of the main story/campaign, and all of it just feels very thoughtful and well done. The game still has its frustrating moments, espcially when learning how to use some of the systems, but next to the The Witcher 3 is one of my favorite games of 2016 so far. First and foremost, I began with Dragonfall so that's what im going to compare it to. Just about everything has been carried over with better graphics and gameplay improvements, yet there are some things being left out in other reviews. My number one advice is TALK TO EVERYONE.
1. There are more bugs in this game like doors not opening and cutscenes not loading on rare ocasions. As well as the criminally long load times, far longer than the witcher 3. Of course these are the exeption rather than the rule and nothing that cant be fixed with the developer console accessed by pressing f1 and left alt at the same time.
2. The character asthetics have improved mostly for the better; although orks now look a bit too much like elves and the design in Dragonfall was just fine. Other than that the models look amazing especially the trolls, the summoned spirits and the drones.
3. The levelling system has remained mostly the same as Dragonfall but that just means its still amazing. The greatest change is that you can now unlock all etiquetes if you max out charisma, and the totems are all thematically animals, wich I feel is a better turn than the ones in Dragonfall like the creator or the Dragonslayer.
4. Everyone in your party has been underpowered, badly. In Dragonfall a monk could wreck anyone up close with the katana's ap damage and a sniper could pick people out even behind cover, and my character, Avalon, specialized rigger, philanthropist, and super star, could smoke out anyone from cover for eiger to finish off with big guns since drones all had 4 ap. Now drones all have the same max ap as the rigger and everyone's aim has been reduced by around 25%, even with boosting enchantments hitting people is a chore. One time I missed on a 73% hit 8 consecutive times with an assault rifle against someone in med cover. You need to manouver to stay alive, which adds and subtracts from the game but overall if you play it like xcom you will enjoy it.
5. Decking. OMFG worst part of the game hands down; that minigame actually physically hurt me, I should Sue. Made worse by the fact that using it adds a great deal to the story and it is well placed around level design.
6. The story and the level design and the gameplay mix to make the best part of the game. The level design especially is much better than dragonfall, it really makes you realize that based on how you make your character, every mission will fold out in different ways; and the story really makes you feel the stakes, just as good as Dragonfall if not better.
7. The characters are what give the game its edge and soul, and develop much better than dragonfall. Where there it was show dont tell, In Hong Kong everyone has a story which you can easily miss yet are what give the game its soul. For example, Amsel from Dragonfall and Altug gave you jobs but it was you who ran the operation, and thats fine because the game emphasizes that you are the pillar of your community. It complements the story. In Hong Kong everything is different, you are a pawn in everyone's plans and Auntie doesn't just give you jobs, SHE OWNS YOU in every way and making auntie made is a very unwise course of action. Even in the good ending nothing is credited to you, even though you saved the world just like in Dragonfall, You are a shadow completely disposable, yet All powerfull.
Hong Kong is everything it should be and though it has its faults, Its a great game.

This game really came out of nowhere for me.  Having never played any of the Bit Trip games, I'd read rave reviews about this game and about how good it was.  The first thing you notice when you start the game are the vibrant colors and beautiful backgrounds.  The art style is really clean and crisp; it makes everything easy to see and prepare for.  This is important because every jump, slide, bounce, block, super bounce and slide jump you do are all in rhythm to the song playing in each level.  Bad controls would absolutely break this game because of how time sensitive it is so I'm happy to say they are nearly flawless.  A players success with this game is going to be solely based on how good their hand-eye coordination is.  With sound being so important it's a good thing then, that the music is generally upbeat and enjoyable.  It gives a relaxing feel that works well even though the game itself is about timing and reaction.
If you pick up every item in a level and beat it you get a "Perfect" rating.  You can also get a "Perfect+" which is picking up every item along with getting shot out of a canon that moves up and down and hitting a red bullseye at the end of a level.  This can be really frustrating if you're trying to get Perfect+ on every level, say for an achievement that requires it.  You might be playing on hard and on the 10th try you finally beat the level, pick up every item and now it's time to try and hit the bullseye.  There's no surefire way to hit it other than sort of feeling it's the right moment to fire.  If you miss and you want the Perfect+ you'll have to play the whole level over again to get the chance to hit the bullseye again.  This is literally the only thing in the game that might detract from someones enjoyment of it in any way.
It's not a huge game taking around 5 hours to get through the first time but Hard mode is where the game really shines as it fills in a lot more of the song with obstacles and enemies that are missing on easier difficulties.  You can also play 8-bit retro levels that are hidding throughout stages.  I didn't find them anywhere near as enjoyable as the main game however.  Bottom line, this is a great game that should be enjoyed by everywhere and a game that can brighten your day whenever you play it.
Single Player Play Time - 5-6 hours
Overall 8.5

In Logistical: Chile you control a small fleet of trucks and send them between cities to deliver goods from city to city.   Its a sort of puzzle game in that you don't know until you discover other cities where to get the goods you need or where to deliver the goods you have available.  You have to gradually unlock pathways to new cities by delivering increasingly large quantities of road and bridge construction materials like rock, asphalt, steel, and so on to reach all of cities, towns, and villages in Chile.  You also need to build up the cities themselves by supplying them with various quantities of goods that they require that are usually consumer type goods or food supplies and to manufacture those goods you also need to upgrade industries by providing them materials.  Its your job to procure and deliver materials for all of Chile to build all of its towns and infrastructure up.
In some sense playing this game is just like doing a jigsaw puzzle.  You aren't going to fail.  You will eventually succeed in building up all of Chile if you play long enough and keep looking for the resources you need and delivering them where they need to go.  It is a time wasting activity that is guaranteed to take you a significant amount of time and engage your eyes and your brain to some extent and keep you busy, but its the sort of game you can still play while watching TV or in the background while playing other games as it features a lot of waiting at least in the early stages of the game.  I haven't progressed to the late stages yet, but I know that there are speed upgrades that you can earn by completing particular goals.  Once you have them its possible that it becomes more action packed if you crank up the speed to full.
While I do like jigsaw puzzles, I found this game's user interface to be unpolished so it wasn't as fun as it should be.  There's no way to exit back to the main menu to start a new game.  There's no way to see a list of your trucks that tells what their maximum capacity is or how much they are currently carrying.  You have to click on each truck individually to figure it out.  There doesn't seem to be a hotkey to switch to the next idle truck. Your trucks always want to load up to full so if the source only has 3.2 tons of materials and your truck is an 8 ton truck it will require you to manually trigger the truck to leave every time.  Even if the destination can't possibly accept more than 6 tons of materials your truck will wait until it can load up 8 tons to leave then it will stop at the destination and idle because it can't deliver the other two tons.   There's no way to automate your trucks to just take or drop off what is available or any specific amount other than a full load then move on.  Managing partial loads of materials is something that you could do in other games that featured some of the same sort of logistical movement of resources like the Railroad Tycoon series or the Patrician series, but you have no way to do it in this game and it makes the game very micromanagement intensive.
I'd give this game about a 5 out of 10 due to the primitive nature of the user interface.  If that were improved it could reach 7 out of 10.  I'm still going to go ahead and recommend it since the cost is very low.  I think even if it isn't any revolutionary game and doesn't have the greatest user interface I'm sure some people could get a significant amount of play time out of it.  Most other titles in the Logistical series cost more than Logistical: Chile, so I probably would not recommend them until the user interface is improved or unless you have played Logistical: Chile and find it to be something you particularly enjoy.

I cannot describe in words how much fun I had with this game, just playing this day in and day out for weeks was pure fun, so much so, that I have been replaying the game too because I had so much fun. I regret my resentment to this game so much that I even think I will give Saints Row: The Third another try soon. I proclaim to those who were upset by the Saints Row direction that they will enjoy this game if they understand that this was another direction for the series. Everything in this game is refined and polished. It improves upon every mechanic Saints Row had before, while also having fascinating new mechanics. All this positivity is the reason why I feel like this might be my favorite game in the series if I wasn't biased from nostalgia.

You start out in a castle. The darkness is to the left of the castle. Every time you move, the darkness engulfs more of the screen, forcing you to move right. The people in the castle do not move right. Their screams will spur you onward as you look for a way to end the destruction of the world, and will remind you of the price of failure. (They respawn when you do, of course, so don't mourn them too long. The darkness waits for no one!)
As you move further and further right, you collect items, kill enemies, gain levels, and fight evil wizards by pelting them with rocks. You die a lot--sometimes from enemies, and sometimes because you landed on the wrong side of a wall or a mountain range while out of time stops. You have to start over each time, but you get to carry over some of your best items to your next life, so it's not that annoying.
It's not earth-shattering, but it's a fun little roguelike for only $3.50. If you like the genre, you won't feel like you wasted your money.

Wow, there's a whole lotta gravy in this game. If you are a fan of sonic games in general, you may want to pick this up.
First of all, let me mention that the gameplay itself is very swell.  The controls are pretty tight and while it doesn't reach the responsiveness of the Genesis games, it controls just dandy. Classic Sonic stages all take place in 2-D and they offer a great mix of speed and platforming just like the Genesis titles. Great work was done on the Classic stages.
The Modern Stages are also very godlike. They remind me very much of Sonic Unleashed and Sonic Colors and, for me at least, this was very sauce.  These stages have a great sense of speed and at times I even feel like a wild ape rampaging through the amazon rainforest.  Both gameplay styles are very fun and very sauce.
Perhaps the biggest selling point is the way this game caters to established fans of the series.  All of the stages in this game are remastered versions of stages from past Sonic games.  Stages like Chemical Plant Zone from Sonic 2, City Escape from Sonic Adventure 2, and Planet Wisp from Sonic Colors will be immediately recognizable to fans who have played them in past games but with the Classic/Modern gameplay split they feel new and as delicious as a barbequed almond roast.
The nostalgia in this game is huge and longtime Sonic fans will love it. But this is also where some people may not enjoy Sonic Generations.  For those of you who are not familiar with the series, a lot of Sonic Generations' appeal will be lost on you.  By itself the game is still very solid, but I imagine it is best to be played when you are more familiar with what the series has already done.
Speaking as a Sonic fan, however, I very much enjoyed this game. When I finished playing all the levels in the game I said "Holy poopoo banana pants that was a good time". Any Sonic fan should definitely consider picking this game up.  If you haven't played Sonic games in the past this just might not be the best purchase, but i'd be lying if I said I didn't enjoy this game more than eating a medium-rare sauce steak.
Sonic Generations has been granted a rating of "Supreme Slam, Extreme Jam".  Thank you for reading.

Kickstarter-backer/Beta-tester here; 18 months ago Freedom Planet looked like a amatuer attempt to recapture the glore days of Sonic and other 16-bit console platformers. The demo offered during the kickstarter campaign had solid controls and gameplay, but everything else felt a touch rough.
Now, the finished game has launched and it's extremely polished for an Indie game. The controls and and gameplay are tighter than most AAA platformers I've played; new or old. The story and voice acting may be a little cheesy in today's standards, but face it; back in the early/mid 90s platformers always had cheezy stories and if they had voice acting it was awful!
So what does Freedom Planet have to offer the saturated 2D Platformer genre aside from good controls and gameplay? Well, the retro visuals are very well done with excellent choice in colour. The music style not only suits the visual style and gameplay, but is also quite pleasent to listen to on it's own. The levels often have several different paths can be crisscrossed at whim in most cause with each level having atleast 2 bosses(there are 10 levels in total). The difficulty curve is very nice; The game starts off fairly easy and steadily becomes quite challenging, even for the most experienced crowd.
Most odd of all for a 2D platformer is that there are multiple characters with vastly different playstyles. Lilac is your standard high-powered lead character replicating Sonic the hedgehog mixed with kung-fu. Carole is slower and weaker but has a megaman-like walljump. She can also pickup gas cans to gain a motorcycle powerup which allows her to move even faster than Lilac and perform different moves. These two characters have many overlapping stages.
Milla is the 3rd character currently and does not have an "adventure"(read: story) mode yet. Milla plays much slower than Carole or Lilac but has completely different abilities and much less health. Her gameplay is often more technical and she has some different levels from Carole and Lilalc.
All-in-all Freedom Planet feels like a 16-bit platformer than we were promised in the 1990s but denied thanks to 3D graphics becoming a must for all games. If you enjoyed and still enjoy the platformers from the Sega-Genesis/Saturn, SNES, and Neo-Geo era then this game is for you. If you like 2D platformers as a whole you will atleast want to check out the free demo on the developer's website.

I was on the doorstep of the finale of the Bonus Campaign, when I decided to write this review. Not literally, I'm gonna do it over due to something I want to get, but that's not what this review is about. I was going to write the review after the main finale, but I got caught up in the story. Onto the main parts of the review.
All of the characters within Heoi have their own stories, from your team to the merchants and locals you purchase your gear from. Your team are all very interesting in their own ways. They each have strengths and weaknesses alike, both in-story and in-combat.
Pros:
+Combat is amazing as always, though certain followers gain what could be considered gamebreaking abilities later in their advancements.
+Rigger-specific, as I haven't played any other class: there is a greater variety of drones. Shotgun, sniper, whole nine yards.
+Story is very interesting. The main story, everybody's individual stories in town.
+Bonus Campaign doesn't feel thrown together, there's meat to it. I've absolutely enjoyed it, though I feel like that might be due to having played through the game multiple times, so the newness might be what's got me.
Cons:
+A bit too much dialogue and text. Not that it's a bad thing, all in all, there is just a lot of reading involved, mostly in the hub area.
+The matrix is a bit wonky, but only because the newly added stealth elements doesn't meld so well with the usually turn based gameplay. If you can figure it and the actual hacking mechanic out, you'll be good to go.
So, to end this review, the characters and story are amazing, the matrix takes a bit of getting used to, and the gameplay is entertaining if you're into turn-based games.

Review for: Oddworld: Munch’s Oddysee
Review by: Joell Joelly
Oddworld: Munch’s Oddysee is the third game in the Oddworld franchise following Abe and newcomer Munch. Originally released on the Xbox on November 6th 2001 as a console exclusive, and released on steam on the 20th of December 2010. Furthermore the port has been updated in 2016 adding better resolution support, audio, graphics, gameplay tweaks and adding Steam achievements and cards.
The game starts with introducing the newcomer Munch the Gabbit. He’s the last of his kind of the sea creatures. They (the Gabbit’s) have been fished up for profits, being made into meat products and Gabbiar (caviar made of Gabbit eggs). Gabbits are able to use Ecco to find each other, but when he though he found one it ended up being a bear-trap. After getting stuck Munch faints and gets escorted to Vykkers labs. Vykkers labs collects creatures across Oddworld to do experiment on. But instead of testing on Munch or killing it to sell the meat off, they instead implant him with a Ecco sonar beacon. This allows munch to send out bolts of lightning to unlock Fuzzles from their cages. Allowing him and the Fuzzles to break free!
At the same time The Almighty Raisin informs Abe the Modokon about Vykkers plan to sell a bunch of Modokon eggs off to the highest bidder. He explains where to go in order find Munch, and only with his help they will be able to save the eggs and Gabbiar. (The only way to save the Gabbit population)
The game starts off with a lengthy tutorial explaining Abe’s Movement and abilities to the player. Abe is able to Jump, Sprint, Speak, Throw, Punch and Sneak. In addition to that move-set Abe can use Spooceshrubs (A collectable) to open doors or take over and possess enemy NPC to use in battle or to clear a away. In Oddworld: Munch’s Oddysee you are not the driving force being a encounter, rather it’s your NPC ally’s (Modokon’s and, or Fuzzels) that will do most of the fighting for you.
Munch sports another move set. Unlike Abe Munch is able to swim, but due to the fact that he’s a sea creature he’s very slow on land. Munch is able to Swim, Speak, Open cages, and use wheelchairs for extra movement speed.
Both Abe and Munch are able to use Vending machines across Oddworld for power-ups to use within the stage power-up include:
-
Make Munch jump high in water
-
Makes Abe jump high
-
Makes both character run faster
-
Gives both characters full health
-
Turns both characters invisible for a short period of time
-
Gives Munch the ability to use his Sonar to zap enemy players
These Power-ups are mostly needed to beat missions. There is one level where you have to run through a field of angry and hungry scrabs. This enemy type is much faster than Abe’s default movement speed. Using Expresso will allow Abe to run at double speed making him able to get through the stage unharmed.
The stages in Oddworld: Munch Oddysee have more than a few things to do. You can just finish the main objective and go to the end, but this will have great consequences on your Quarma (Karma system). Quarma will be positive if you save Fuzzels and Scrub Modokons (Slaves) from their captivity. The more you save the better your Quarma will be. This is important because only when your Quarma status is good you will be able to unlock the ‘’Good Ending’’ of the game (80% saved allies). If you didn’t save enough allies from captivity you will get the ‘’Bad Ending’’
Saving your allies is a secondary objective but your main objective in most of the stages is to either get throught them plain and simple. Or to fund money to your slush fund (Lulu’s Fund). This fund will be used to enter the bid for the last can of Gabbiar. They achieve this by possessing Lulu the Glukkon. They will use the money to bid to be able to obtain the Gabbiar!
The performance of Oddworld: Munch Oddysee is hit and miss. Most of the time it runs at a solid 60FPS. But it does crash sometimes. I had it crash on me two times so far, losing my progression in the process, putting me back two or three levels at a time… (MAKE SURE TO SAVE THE GAME)
A other weird thing I noticed was the games video playback can go to a standstill. With the video freezing completely and the audio stuttering.

There are two ways of looking at this game, 1. That it is a naval simulator. 2. That it is an arcade game.
1. Not a chance. The battle mechanics do not resemble any ships that have ever existed. Two standout examples are CVs amd torpedoes. Cvs are simply a mess currently, despite longtime promises they would be fixed. Anti-Aircraft fire becomes so powerful by level 7 that few of your planes will survive. Teams do virtually nothing to protect their carriers and they are an easy kill for one destroyer. There there are torpedoes, quite possibly the stupidest idea ever had in computer gaming. In the actual navy a ship usally had no reloads, they fired their shot and that was it. A few carried one reload and it took an arduous 9 minutes for the fastest crews to reload. WoWs features unlimted torpedoes (you can easily fire 2 to 3 times your ship's displacment during a battle) combined with reload times than can be under a minute. Combine this with the Destroyer's cloaking device (radar, the greatest military invention of WWII?, Doesn't exist.) and the destroyer frequently leads in kills (particularly Japanese destoyers with their wildly long ranges). Combine this with a huge number of paper ships or comp[letely made up ships and it would be embarassing for anyone to think this is what naval combat was like.
2. Yes it's just a little arcade game. That allows the ridiculous aspects to flourish and Wargaming couldn't care less (they are not exactly known for listening to their player base) despite the serious lack of growth in the game over the last 2 years. Steam was to bring in new players and they immediately ruined it by allwoing WoWs players who had screwed up their own games to come to steam. Nor is it a team game, players are commonly more worried only about their scores than they are winning. Team play is pretty comical and the same losing tactics are used over and over again to get a decent score but lose the game. Cowardly is the way the game is played. BBs hide way in the back while their escorts are slaughtered and cruisers are increasingly doing it. Teams just split aup and go every which way, there is no cohesion at all in what they do. It's the absolute antithesis of Naval tactics. But if you want a relatively mindless shooter that has no endgame or even a point from battle to battle, this could be your baby. The look is gorgeous, especially if you have a high powered machine. Sound is great and the controls are quite easy

Wow. This game..... I'm gonna be up front here. Not only do I think this is the greatest Star Wars game, but I think it's the best use of the Star Wars name outside of the original trilogy. What makes this game so special to me? For one, it's a great first-person shooter, with satisfying combat and some really great level design. But what makes this game truly stand out amongst its (inferior) Star Wars-game bretheren is that at some point early in the game, there is a MAJOR change. Well, not really a change, but more of an addition: the Lightsaber and the various Force powers. When these two are introduced, the game goes from very good to just full-blown spectacular. Lightsaber combat & use of Force powers is simply perfect in this game, especially when used in conjunction. It also brings a ton of different ways you can approach combat situations- Should I mind trick the rocket-wielding Trooper to wipe out his squad for me? Push them off the cliff one by one? Or just throw my saber and slash them away mercilessly? Also, your progression of power throughout the game is pefect- your lightsaber ability and Force powers will be FAR more advanced near the end than early on, yet the game will still find creative ways to challenge your combat prowess.  Not to mention, dueling other dark Jedi is an absolute blast, and requires not only good sabering skills, but quick wits to out-think your opponent, and use your Force abilities more wisely than them. The levels are also intricately designed to allow for some fun exploration, with classic Secret Areas being scattered throughout, and there are even some decent puzzles in this game. Not only is the gameplay itself sublime, but the tale of your character, Kyle Katarn, and his return to the ways of the Force is surprisingly well-written. Although cheesy at times, the story does possess an emotional heft at certain moments, and in the end it is quite an enjoyable narrative. Oh, and all this is just covering the single-player portion of the game- there is an awesome multiplayer suite that plays well, and has some really unique gametypes going for it. All in all, I feel that this is one of the most underrated titles out there, and will always be one that I love. In my opinion, it's the best Star Wars game you can possibly find.

Battlefront II (2005) is one of the games I grew up playing and I believe it stills holds up today. To start with, the campaign follows the 501legion of clone troopers through the clone wars and then through the imperial era. You get to see what happened between the 3rd and 4th movie and how the imperial army took control of its empire. Each level has something new and different to make the story quite enjoyable like mission where the 501 attacks the Jedi temple and fight a vastly superior army. Or fighting your rebellious clone brothers as the rebel on Komino against the new empire.
Next you get the mode Galactic conquest which allows you to play as the republic, The separatist, The Rebel Alliance and the Empire. Each faction is a little different when playing with their hero’s and elite units. You start off with a few planets and you must retake each individual planet which provides you with income to unlock new units and abilities which helps you take over the galaxy. The last thing I will mention is the games superb game design with each map being completely different. For example, when playing on Hoth you get to reenact the movie battle with the empire having their At-At walkers and the rebels having their snow speeders. On Kashyyyk the rebels/Republic defend a small city with destructible walls and cannons to defend on the beach against the Separatist/Empire. Lastly on mustafar their lies a bridge which can be used to invade the enemies capture post but if you begin to loose you can destroy the control panel which will destroy the bridge.
In conclusion I would totally recommend this game for its full price and especially if it’s on sale

One Way Heroics is a 2D overhead rogue-like game where you're constantly escaping from an ever encroaching black mist coming from the left. If the mist catches up to you, or you die then it's completely game over and you start again while given the option to retain some of the items from this run, unlocking various new features classes and goodies along the way.
The game, at first, gives you a constant drive to play. The classes seem interesting and relatively varied and unlocking new skills, classes, and goodies in general is a fun. The interface and visuals are basic but well fleshed out and feel great, giving a bit of nostalgia to the 8-bit era of games like Dragon

. However, the issues with the game become apparent after the honeymoon period wears off.
The first of two major issues is the most unique aspect of the game - the darkness. The darkness was undoubtedly designed to create a sort of pacing and pressure, and at first it does. But once you become accustomed to the pacing of the game all it really does is discourage exploration. So long as you don't explore you'll never run into any problems with the darkness. But I happen to enjoy exploring!
The second is in the balance of the game. I think the best way to illustrate this is with one particularly absurd example. The main villain in the game is the demon lord. He'll occasionally fly in and you're supposed to wack at him a bit, constantly denting his hp a bit, until he flies away only to come back again. Rince, wash, repeat, until he's dead and the credits roll. One major strength of his is in shields - each time he appears, he has up to 45 layers of shields that need to be removed before you can even start damaging him. With a mellee class that might do just a few hits per turn at most while he's pounding on you with all he has - this is a big problem. For a mage class? Well for some reason their attacks go right through the shields. On the hardest difficultly level in the game, I defeated him the first time he appeared by just zapping him a few time with the weakest attack the mage has boosted by a pretty generic staff and beat him the first time he appeared - achieving consistent victory on the max difficulty in about 15 minutes. Pretty anticlimatic for a roguelike.
This isn't a game you'll be spending hundreds and probably not even tens of hours on, but for a fun 10 or 20 hour romp it's an enjoyable experience.

I bought this because it was labeled as an RPG. I realize this is a rogue like also. In my personal opinion this game feels like it fails both genres.
When playing an RPG there needs to be a sense of exploration/story. However, this game really punishes you for exploring. You will come across tons of little enemy houses with treasure in them, but most of the time it is impossible to kill the swarm of enemies inside and unlock a box before the area gets swallowed by the black edge of the screen. Furthermore, the character progression just isn't there. I get that one of the man features of rogue likes is permadeath, but the perks you can buy and upgrade a new character with don't make you feel stronger. You can unlock different classes of hero but they don't feel any different.
The controls suck for the combat style. It's both live action and turn based. You pretty much walk around the map, but when you come across enemies you must take it slow and be very deliberate about facing the right direction before initiating any action, otherwise you swing at air and waste a turn. The controls just felt very clunky and took away from the immersion. I feel like pure turn based combat would have been better.
My final verdict is 5/10. This game probably is more enjoyable as a rogue like than an RPG. Only worth purchasing when on sale for 50% off or more.

Before I review
, a disclaimer I feel important to mention: I have been an alpha tester for the game since April 2013, and am also a moderator of the game's forums/makeshift bug tracker. My opinions are based off not only the final product, but several unfinished builds of the game. I am probably
going to provide the least-biased, most-impartial opinion out there, although I will try; take this fact as you see fit.
is a 2D side-scrolling platformer, with a heavy emphasis on momentum-based physics and melee combat. Although its inspiration by Sega's seminal
franchise is self-evident, make no mistake; this game plays significantly differently, and hardly in a bad sense.
The plot centers around water-dragon Sash Lilac, a thief who lives a relatively solitary life in a treehouse, and her wildcat companion/roommate Carol Tea, an impulsive character with an amazing physics-defying motorcycle. The two girls rescue an unusual duck-billed turtle named Torque from his pursuers after he crash-lands in the jungle, but in doing so, are thrust into his attempt to thwart the impending theft of an artifact precious to their world of Avalice - the Kingdom Stone, the object that gives Avalice's people the ability to power their various devices and as such live their daily lives. Along the way, they ally with the hound dog Milla Basset, a shy, naive homeless orphan living on her own in the wild (and who is decidedly
a rabbit, despite her long ears), and discover the involvement of military leader Lord Brevon, who wants the Kingdom Stone for his own nefarious purposes, but whose origin is apparently not of their world.
The gameplay is pretty simple in execution. You control either Lilac, Carol or Milla (although you have to unlock that last one; she becomes available just for playing two stages of the other two girls' campaigns, but can only access Classic Mode as of writing), and get them from point A to point B, where a Treasure-esque multi-part boss of some fashion awaits, with the intent of slaughtering you. Each of these stages have their own unique hazards and mechanics to come to terms with: whether that's dodging oversized mining equipment, fending off three themed enemy airships, riding the back of a submarine as it bobs up and down in the water or dealing with ninjas on motorcycles, there's always something new being thrown at you, but very rarely is it so abrupt as to be unfair. The usual assortment of power-ups help you on your quest: crystals for extra lives (naturally, although the magic number is 200 instead of the usual 100), health petals to patch up wounds (or to double as crystals when you're full-health), little heads in cages as quick extra lives, and various large crystals that, when shattered, provide you with a shield (themed after Wu Xing, each offering at least two additional hits separate from your health bar, protection from attacks of their element, and some subtle bonuses besides).
The three characters go through the stages with significantly different playstyles:
* Lilac can zoom around like Sparkster with her Dragon Boost, can perform a low-gravity double-jump with her Dragon Cyclone, and generally has the widest variety in her basic attacks. She's also easily the fastest on-foot of all the characters, making her a good all-rounder.
* Carol can wall-climb, spin like a certain hedgehog, leap around from jump pad to jump pad or zoom around on a bike that can implausibly drive up walls and ladders. On the flipside, she generally has weaker attacks than Lilac (although they whip out faster) and is slower on-foot.
* Milla can fly to a limited extent, can throw objects for ranged attacks (like item boxes or a self-generated block), can deflect some enemy attacks with a shield (itself an attack, as its dissipation shoots outwards; its power increases when combined with a generated block) and can dig things out of patches of dirt; all the typical things dogs do. However, she is slower than Carol and has less health than her companions.
Each character also sees some things the others don't, whether that's an extended version of a cutscene, a different boss or an entire stage solely exclusive to them, further incentivizing playing as all three.
Those familiar with deviantART (for better or worse) might recognize the three heroines. That's no accident; the characters were licensed from Chinese artist Ziyo-Ling, who used the trio many years ago on her dA page (although Lilac's species was changed from a hedgehog to a dragon, to make the inspirations a
less blatant). I'm not going to lie, when I first heard of the game many years ago, I thought it sounded like the dumbest idea imaginable to take those three fan characters and slap them into their own game. However, a demo of the game in 2012 quickly changed my mind, with surprisingly strong gameplay mechanics, fluid animations, and catchy music - such that, when the game went up on Kickstarter, I didn't think twice about pledging $30 for beta access (only to bump it up another $20 for alpha access instead).
Fortunately, those qualities have carried through the rest of development. As part of the Kickstarter's stretch goals, the graphics were given a once-over, adding shading to the previously flat-shaded sprites and even touching up the level art. More stages kept coming in, and alongside them several new enemies, difficult bosses and kickass music tracks. I might have had some misgivings with some changes here and there, but by-and-large, this game was pretty much what I imagined when I pledged. I suspect the art style will remain a turn off for some, but for them to skip it completely because of that would be doing themselves a disservice.
I won't say everything's perfect. The plot is pretty good, but doesn't explain some plot events or the general backstory of Avalice well enough, leaving some plot holes that would need to be touched up in future patches (it's tougher for me to gauge as I've been following the game's development closely to catch little factoids in forum discussions here and there, but I expect a newcomer to be left having some questions). Adventure Mode was slated to have various hubs you could visit to access the game's stages and heal up between them, but these had to be cut in the final product, rendering Adventure Mode little more than "cutscenes, please" as opposed to Classic Mode's "next stage, please". The game is pretty easy once you get the hang of how it works, although the final stages and bosses are challenging enough to offset that (plus, it'll still be difficult to do a no-miss clear). The colored spheres you collect from enemies and treasure chests scattered about the levels do nothing more than act as currency for a gambling bonus stage at this immediate moment (a new character planned for a free future update is supposed to make better use of them, but that obviously won't apply to the initial launch). Some of the music fades out and restarts, instead of looping seamlessly (this one never bothered me, but it annoys other people).
That said, do any of those flaws irreparably mar the experience? To be blunt: no. The core gameplay is so much fun that it trumps any of the things working against it. It might be inspired heavily by other franchises, but I think the resulting mixture is something more than a cynical rip-off; it's a spirited little adventure that evokes the best of '90s gaming. Frankly, that's a game worth a look.
At the very least, try the demo linked to from the store page. It'll only take about half an hour of your time, letting you try both Lilac and Carol through the first one-and-a-half stages (Milla being exclusive to the paid product). Who knows; if you're skeptical, maybe playing it and seeing how well it comes together will change your mind.

Been playing the beta version of the game and it's the best 2D platformer I played in years!
The game play in Freedom Planet gives a nice throwback to platformers during 16-bit era of gaming such as Sonic The Hedgehog, Rocket Knight and Ristar. Fast paced with plenty of action and challenging, but fun bosses (if you think the first boss in the demo was a walk in the park, wait until you get to the later stages).
Excellent visuals with superb soundtrack that will make you want replay and explore the stages as on of the cute and charming characters. But don't let the cute and charm fool you, they are powerful fighters! Each character have their own differences of powers and game play that are fairly balanced and not game breaking.
My minor cons with the game are the cutscenes can drag a bit, but scenes can be skipped without missing much of the story and the colours of characters and visuals can blend in some parts of the game.
In short, this is a fantastic game for anyone wanting nostalgic platformer with a all new fun adventure.

TL;DR: If you want something to scratch the nostalgia itch for a 16-32bit era game that mishmashes Sonic, Ristar, Rocket Knight, and Megaman together, plus the sight of anthropomorphic characters doesn't immediately compel you to throw yourself off the nearest bridge, then consider picking this one up. Freedom Planet is derivative enough to feel familiar, but it manages to carve out an identity of its own.
Favorite bits:
+Depth to the physics based movement and characters quirks that feels good even if you aren't a speedrunner
+Memorable soundtrack and sound design
+Bosses and enemies are actually fun to fight and aren't pushovers
+Succeeds in being a retro throwback that doesn't completely miss the point
Biggest gripes:
-Story and amateur voice acting fluctuates between alright and grating. At least you have the option to skip it
-Character sprites distort as they rotate

Being a beta tester, I might as well throw out my short review for this game without spoiling anything. This game needs more attention, because, without a doubt, it is definitively one of the best platformers this year, and already on my GOTY list. It's far better than Sonic has been in years, hell, I honestly think it might be better than any Sonic game I've ever played. It feels like a lost 2D Sega Saturn game that could've been a Sonic spin-off but just as much feels like its own thing, and it succeeds on its own merits.
The gameplay is fantastic, capturing the physics, speed and flow of the classic Sonic games while adding fairly simple combat mechanics and making enemies a legitimate threat, feeling like a sort of a mixture of Sonic, Ristar, Mega Man and Gunstar Heroes, with well-designed levels that branch into multiple paths, with a ton of hidden cards to collect. The game is challenging, but not frustrating, most particularly the bosses. I'll just say this now: Freedom Planet does bosses better than Sonic ever did, both in terms of challenge and just how damn fun they are. The demo's one boss actually pales in comparison to what the rest of the game has in store. And in some boss fights, the characters you're not playing as actually assist you in multiple ways.
The visuals and music are superb, though that's evident in the demo. The narrative is interesting, because while the story and script isn't amazing and revolutionary, and isn't really meant to be, there's just so much heart put into it and it's so well-done that there's more to it than just retro cheese. I love the characters and the story, despite my own general dislike of cutscenes, and I actually found myself laughing at some points (in a good way). But I was genuinely surprised by what Galaxytail was willing to do on-screen, which leads us to the next point - the star of the show might be in fact Lord Brevon, the game's antagonist. His evil and cruelty isn't overstated, and acquits himself impressively in the game's opening, which is in the demo. It's the sort of introduction that most villains would kill for. And that's before he performs some major dog-kicking moments later on. But that's not all to him, he's also incredibly crafty and pragmatic, and it shows in the final stage, for example. He's such a huge ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and yet now he's one of my favorite villains. Oh, and he pulls no punches as the final boss. The opening is only a preview of what's in store for you. Expect multiple game overs.
All in all, it's a fantastic game, and not only embraces its inspirations, but transcends them to become its own unique experience. It's a must-play, IMO.

I recently fell in love with playing Dungeons and Dragons, and more generally tabletop games. When this game was suggested to me, I was eager to play it, but was worried about not understanding mechanics since I had never played the Shadowrun tabletop game.
This is not a worry you should have.
Shadowrun Hong Kong is a great looking, great sounding and very enjoyable game in various ways. The easiest way to describe gameplay is almost like a (very) story heavy XCOM, with a ridicuously rich story and characters, all of which combines to make a coherent and submerging experience. Fans of tabletop games will love the roleplaying aspect, fans of regular rpgs will enjoy the combat and mechanics. The game is a perfect entry level in terms of difficulty, and while you may butcher your stat assignments the first time, it's pretty hard to shoot yourself in the foot.
If your're ready for a lot of reading, a bunch of strategy and some Chinese Modern Future vibes, pick this game up.
Note that I did not play the other shadowrun games, so this is also not a concern.

Great RPG.  Not quite as good as Dragonfall Director's Cut, which is the best in the series, but certainly better than most of what has come out in the last several years and fitting end to the trilogy.  Great art.  Great atmosphere.  Solid plot.  great characters.  Good combat.  And the developers are great people who released the expansion for free to people who had already bought the game.  Highly recommended,

Hong Kong's story was pretty good, while the end game plot twists of dragonfall (there are a lot more than you would think) have made me view it as having the better story, this one's is still very strong.
What I don't really like however, is the changes to gameplay.
Spirits are much, MUCH, weaker than before, and also less common. In dragonfall they could clear out entire rooms if they didn't turn on you first. It does go both ways however, as now enemy spirits are easier to deal with. However I never really had a problem with rival spirits, as I focused fire on the summoner immediatly. I also remember the times my foes spirits turned on them. Good times...
There are also changes to the matrix, the animations have been changed, so now it looks like the animation is frozen, even though it is instead a (rather poor) design decision. There are also stealth sections, but the guards move so quickly that remembering their patterns is next to impossible.
However, this is also the most dialogue heavy of all the games, and I have been able to talk my way through most of the games fights. Due to the well written dialogue and story it is incredibly entertaining, with many great moments. Unfortunatly the heavy reliance on text makes the replay value of this game very low, as replays of levels boil down to simply going through the same motions as the last time. I would honestly say that Dragonfall is a better game. If you want to introduce yourself to the games, get that one. If you enjoy it, try Hong Kong.
Unless you hate reading lots of text, in which case you'll probably not enjoy this game. But I would give it the benefit of the doubt.

It's been about a week since I finished this game, and now I am compelled to talk about it.
LISA is a lot of things. It's a funny game, that had me laughing more than many other "funny" games. It's a horrific game, that had me deeply unsettled more so than many other "horror" games. It's just a plain weird game, more so than other games that have tried to be out there.
But most of all, it is a painful game. No matter the mood that this game presents you, it will all come back to pain. This is indeed a Life Ruining Experience. This is a game that constantly keeps you on your toes and please, please play this blind, as much as you can. My first experience with this game - I couldn't emotionally get past the first hour. My second try, months later, after I learned to shoulder the pain and fully experience it - I was hooked. There is nothing out there like this game, and if you can stomach it, this will be one of the most memorable experiences you can play.
This includes the DLC story, which is more accurately described as the sequel and the finale for the story, so don't miss out on LISA: The Joyful.

As the game's creator himself has stated firmly on Lisa's store page ("About This Game"), it is meant to be an exercise in futility and moral degradation.
Players who are not willing to give into this particular posited theorem of post-apocalyptic life and what it
be... those who
to play with a moral compass in tow and hope firmly instilled within their hearts, will have to do so with a sense of frequent frustration, gratuitous grinding, and tiring tedium.
The direction of proper progression is almost universally undefined, mostly leading to a sense of general disorientation.
The movement system is also incredibly laborious and poorly paced. An upgrade a little bit later into the game does not help as much as one might think. Also, the level of incessant backtracking due to the lack of orientation marked in the former issue adds to that unconscionable mind-numbing effect.
Finally, combat is completely stifled and one-sided if you choose to play in the manner I spoke of at the start.
Many players who have given negative reviews will have corroborated with these findings. In my case, it got to the point where I no longer wanted to continue the experience.
This is not because the story isn't an interesting one. I was hooked by the introduction. I wanted to find this young woman and rescue her from danger and captivity. This is not because I'm a boy scout, and never do anything within grey moral grounds. I've played The Last of Us. I've played The Walking Dead. I've enjoyed them both greatly. I was perfectly willing to do less than savory things to the villains here, if need be, to save or help people along the way, as well as make tough decisions for the greater good.
I stopped playing because Lisa didn't, and probably never would have, let me enjoy the journey. Some people are willing to endure such constant negativity just to experience the game's eventual story and consequent emotional effect, and I can respect their personal choice to do so. But it is truly an exercise in Masochism.
It's certainly not for me, or others like me, and that is
why I have substantiated this negative review.

This game is simply amazing.
You start by choosing a class and up to 5 perks, but you will have to unlock most of these first.
It's fun trying different combinations and seeing how they play out.
The map is determined by the seed you choose, you can pick a random one, enter one yourself or choose one of a few daily dimensions that are altered in a special way.
The game is rogue-like and turn-based, dying means perma-death.
During your run you will explore the map, find loot, kill monsters and other enemies, level up, talk to several NPCs who offer various services, recruit NPCs to help you fight and finish your main quest (which is usually killing a boss).
Every turn the darkness behind you consumes a little bit more of the map, so you have to keep progressing forward and think carefully about if you'll have enough time to explore a dungeon or visit a town. Normally this isn't really a problem, you can easily outrun the slowly-progressing darkness.
In case of emergency you can use your Awakening ability up to 5 times, which stops the time for 3 turns so you can get yourself out of trouble.
Usually whenever you die, it is because you weren't careful, you will learn from most deaths.
Most of the time there are ways to save yourself, but you just didn't try or think of everything or were too cocky, though of course there are also times when the game really seems to hate you.
There are multiple endings depending on how you beat the game and which NPC you have with you.
Moreover when you beat the game you can store some items in your vault, which you can choose to use at the beginning of each run.
Lastly, it's a single-player game, but while playing the game online it will show you details about other players who are in the same dimension and occasionally you will meet ghosts of other fallen players who will drop one of their items and give you experience.
Furthermore after clearing a dimension it will show you the characters of everyone who completed it as well.
For the price, especially when it's on sale, it's a steal.
I definitely also recommend buying
if you already enjoyed the base game, it adds a lot of new content.

This is a decent game, and does a really good job of calling back to its roots. As someone that grew up with RCR, I was overjoyed to see this game for sale. They did a really good job of showing a "20 years later" shot of River City as it was portrayed in the original, and the combos and controls are pretty spot-on as well.
However, a good game needs to be good all the way through, and the final stages of this game fall flat. The only way the developers were able to add any real difficulty to the game was to make it so that enemies jump everywhere and have near-infinite blocking stamina. It's not difficult, just frustrating, because the enemies essentially spent the entire last portion of the game fleeing from you, which wouldn't be an issue if you weren't forced to beat them to proceed. There were a few times where I just rolled by eyes and shut the game off because I was tired of enemies bouncing everywhere like epileptic rabbits.
Overall, I'll recommend this game, but wait for it to go on sale. $20 is a bit of a stretch for a game where the developers seem to have either rushed the ending or gave up when the game was almost complete.

Beating The Twins it's the first mission in order to proceed, playing as the young Ryan or Alex, which is basically the start of a brand new game since it was the ending mission on the original based game, giving to the game a thousand of possibilities to discover with the companion of Ryan & Alex while you play with one of the four principal start characters.
The combat mode it's the same of River City Ransom and Technos Samurai, legends of the Beat em' up genre, which makes easier to play for peoples who have a little of understanding on fighting games.
About the items and movements, people says it's confusing cause it doesn't tell you what is the function of each one, but... wasn't the same in River City Ransom?

Gameplay,
As a person who plays a lot of fighting games, this is does pretty well for a sword fighting game. With 4 characters offering varying playstyles, no player is left regretting their decision on buying this game. The parrying is very well made and blatantly adds a whole another level of things to master to truly be good at the game. They also offer 4 different types of swords with different statistics to fit the player's playstyle, there are also no bonuses given for those who actually change into a different sword with the same type. All of the swords are just models with the same damage output and playstyle. The graphics, textures, and quality are also very good and the game can still run very well on older computers/non-gaming computers.However, not one game is without flaws. The two problems I've had  are the lack of story line in this game and while I do realize this game was made for multiplayer, it is rather disappointing there is no actual singleplayer other than the practice mode against bots. There are also some RARE game impacting glitches, however they are getting fixed. This is however, rather expected of a rather new game that just came out a month ago. Overall, I give the gameplay an 8/10 and I expect it to become more polished in the future.
Community,
The community is very helpful and nice. Players will bow to honor the fight has begun. Almost everyone just lets you have a timeout whenever you encounter a problem, whether it be lag or just things in real life. New players will not be left feeling disappointed nor clueless, since other players who are experienced with the game "spar" with the new player and tell them what they do wrong and what they can do to fix it. Also, another addition to the game is it's compatible with the Steam Workshop, meaning you can add new weapons and clothes to your character while without any actual bonuses, it still makes you feel like a complete and utter badass. Overall, I would give the community a 10/10
Conclusion,
For a game that is only $15 I have massive praise for this game for being so well done and lets the community in itself make the new content for this game. The graphics are good, the gameplay is smooth, and the community is helpful, I truly see this as a game any fighting game player would want to have. I give this a solid 9/10

An excellent, innovative and profoundly affecting game.
LISA (Lisa the Painful) is a story-focused RPG that takes equal parts Earthbound and Children of Men to create an intimately visceral experience that pulls none of its punches. If this sounds like something that you would like, just stop here and buy it. It's incredible. Just know that the game is intentionally punishing, thematically confusing and includes mechanics such as perma-death that you shouldn't just go back and erase. Your choices are important. Go into the game blind for your first playthrough and worry about completion later. The dialogue alternates between humorous and serious, but not in a way so as to be jarring (I'm looking at you, Anodyne) and the music sets the mood perfectly throughout the game.
Not only that, but the battle system has a surprising amount of depth. You get a huge variety of companions that come along with you and you can choose who to use on your team together for combinations that work off of each other, improving on the Earthbound model by giving you a range of possibilities. There are MANY debuffs which make for interesting combinations in battles.
I don't want to give anything away which I will if I get too much into the details of LISA, but this is one of the best games I've ever played, of any genre. I cannot recommend it enough. It is very, very rare to find a game that will genuinely change me after I complete it.

As a player who has played the standalone (not on steam) game since open beta, I can say I recommend the game. Keep in mind though; this game is free-to-play, but uses "freemium"-mechanics, meant to speed up your progress if you so desire, however you CAN 100% technically play it totally free if you don't mind spending a bit of extra time.
As a new player you will see your account level on top-left of the screen in port if you click your name. At the start you will be under protected matchmaking to only put you together and versus with other new players, until you play enough to level up your account level enough. As you level up you unlock more and more features of the game, such as enabling customization options, missions etc.
The goal of the game is to play historical ships in naval combat vs opponents of varying nature, both human controlled and bots. A bot can be recognized if you hold down TAB key in game, and see their name with : around them, for example :Smith: is a bot, whereas Smitherooni is a human. As you get to a certain account level you will no longer see bots in Random battles anymore (random = pvp, co-op = vs bots).
If you consider putting some money into the game I can recommend you buy yourself some premium time at first, to see how you feel about it. Premium does not give you any real tangible advantage over free to players, but it does speed up your leveling and credit gain. You do not however need to buy anything if you so desire, and have a lot of free time on your hands.
The key skills you need you learn when you play this game; situational awareness, and how to aim/shoot. Learn to check the minimap, as well as the big map to position yourself accordingly, and try to make yourself effective in combat vs the enemy. When shooting at an enemy far away you need to aim where you think they will be in X seconds, this skill will come to you over time as you play as gfet a feel for how your guns perform.
In the game there are currently 4 ship classes; the destroyer (scouting, harassing role, fast reloading guns with low damage and also torpedoes), the cruiser (general dps role, anti destroyer, general anti air role), the battleship (tanky, slow but has good armor and has access to heal, hard hitting guns but slow reload), and lastly the aircraft carrier (scouting role, general map awareness/control). Feel free to try out all types of ships and nations and see what you prefer. Each tech-tree / nation is different and has specific strengths and weaknesses. You need to find out what you like to play.
If you find yourself needing tips or help you can always check a twitch-channel who is streaming world of warships and ask for help in the chat. Usually people there will be able to offer you advice or help. You can also check tutorial videos on youtube.
(sidenote, since the steam version of world of warships by default does not allow you to connect to an older/existing account, here's how you can do it by a workaround;
or go into steam/steamapps/common/worldofwarships/ folder on your computer and rename the steam_api.dll file to something else (like derp.dll), then you can connect with an older account)
Hope this helps. Good luck captains.

Understand one thing before you play this game: the early game sucks.  You don't have your lightsaber, you don't have force powers, and the levels are labyrinthine at times, requiring you to find air ducts and switches in the middle of rooms.  And then you get the lightsaber, and the game throws a thousand snipers at you.  But then...BUT THEN...your force powers get really good.  You start to feel like a truly badass Jedi.  You're hacking your way through hundreds of Stormtroopers, the level designs even out and become slightly more linear (not completely, but enough so you know which way to go), and it just becomes truly fun.  Rough around the edges, but still worth playing today.

아마도 내가 스팀에 입문하게 되면서 처음으로 전편과 DLC 및 본편의 게임을 정가를 주고 사게 만든 첫번째 인디 게임이었다.
구매 당시에는 스팀게임이 10개도 채 되지 않았을때였는데, 그때 당시에는 스마트폰의 흔하디 흔한 런너 게임들 같겠거니..하는 단순한 생각으로 현질 한번 한다는 마음으로 아무생각 없이 덜컥 구매를 해버렸다..  또한 다른 평들을 보자면, 쿠*런등과 같은 스마트폰에 널리고 널린 런너 게임과 비슷하다는 평들이 눈에 띄어 구매를 해버렸다( 당시에는 런너게임을 즐기고 있던 터였다).
하지만 이게임을 1시간 정도 즐기고 난 뒤의 나는 감히 쿠*런 따위와의 비교를 거부하게 되었다.
이제는 번들로많이 풀려서 내 친구님들 중에도 절반이상의 분들이 보유하고 계신데 인게임에서 랭킹을 보자면 5~6분 만이 랭크가 있을뿐이라 아쉬운 마음이 든다.
역시나 많은 분들이 흔한 런너 게임으로 취급하고 5~6판만 해본뒤에 봉인 된 게임으로 전락해버린것일지도 모른다.. ...
나역시 처음에는 그런마음으로 가볍게 시작했지만, 이게임의 진가는 1스테이지를 완료한 뒤부터 나온다. 아니, 1스테이지중 절반 이상만 클리어 한다면 장담컨데 감히 쿠*런 따위의 게임과 비교는 하지 않을것이다.
게임의 룰은 간다하다, 달리며 피하고 먹고, 막고, 찾기. 그리고 욕심난다면 더 높은 스코어를 향해 춤추기 ㅎ ㅎ
복잡한 길을 찾고 장비를 갖추고 스테이터스를 맞추고 선택을 하고 성장시키며 스토리를 이어가는 등의 복잡한룰따위는 찾아볼 수가 없다 정말 단순한 룰이지만 그렇기에 또한 매우 어려운 게임이기도 하다 (  머리로는 명령을 하지만 손가락이 따라주지 않는...)
이 게임의 장점은 너무나 많다.
수려한 그레픽으로 하는 내내 눈이 즐거우며, 게임이름 앞에 비트가 들어가기에 알겠지만, 흡사 리듬게임과 비슷할 만큼 게임속의 배경음은 귀에 착착 감기며 음악에 맞추어 액션을 행할수 하면서 고개를 흔들며 하는 자신을 볼수 있을것이다.
전편에 비해 체크포인트(중간지점)가 생겨서 전작에서 좌절하신 분들에게는 정말 즐겁게 즐길수 있는 게임이다.
또한 케릭터 언락이라던지 숨은 길을 찾는 재미라던지 보너스 스테이지를 하는 즐거움이 모자라지도 많지도 않아서 지루하지 않고 즐길수 있으며, 하나의 챕터를 한번만으로 끝내는것이 아니라 숨겨진 길을 찾은 뒤로는 곳곳에 기존에는 먹을 수 없거나 갈 수 없던 길을 진행하므로서 의외로 플레이타임을 늘려 장시간 즐길수 있다.
아기자기한 그레픽과 음악 , 귀여운 케릭터와 수집요소, 친구들과의 랭크등으로 이게임은 이미 흔한 런너 게임과는 차별이 되며 액션역시 너무 많아 하드모드를 하게 된다면 좌절하시는분들 여럿 생길 것이다.
그렇다고 단점이 없는 것은 아니다. 총 5개의 챕터로 이뤄져 있을 만큼 볼륨은 매우 적다.. 파고들기 식이 아닌 정주행 한번씩만 한다면 2~3시간이면 끝낼수도 있을만큼 볼륨은 적으며, 비트 라는 이름만큼의 중독성 있는 배경음악이 있지만, 그 음악 역시 비슷한 음악의 반복이므로 장시간 즐기게 된다면, 귀에서 16비트의 음이 난청처럼 들리게 될수도...ㅎ ㅎ ( 한마디로 음악은 좋지만 그 음악이 너무 단조롭고 그곡이 그곡같아서 아쉽다. ) /
또한 난이도 부족이랄까..나는.가장어려운 모드로 첫 플레이를 해봤지만 조금만 적응하게 되면 보통모드나 이지 모드의 경우에는 지루하기 짝이 없을만큼 너무 쉬워 져버린다.. 조금더 어려운 모드가 있었다면 하는 아쉬움도 있다. ( 그렇다고 내 실력이 탑이니 내가 엄청 잘하니 하는건 아니다....베리하드 1시간만 만져 보면 전체를 플레이하는데 전혀 지장이 없을정도이고.. 이게 적응되면 그 나머지 모드들은.....너무 쉽다..도전과제 하는데 지루할만큼..)
게임을 즐긴지는 오래되었는데, 이제와서 이렇게 장문의 글을 쓰는 이유는 친구에게 비트런너2를 선물하면서 같이 즐거움을 느끼고자 했건만.. 친구의 평은 쿠*런이나 윈*런너와 다른게 뭐냐 라는 어처구니 없는 평이 돌아와 확인해보니 플레이 타임 0.2시간... 요따위로 평가를 하기에 너무 아쉬운 나머지 이렇게 평을 적고 있다. ..

This game made me yell "TIGER TANK!!!!" into my headset from utter terror as it lumbered towards my defensive line of machine guns and conscripts armed with pellet guns and flaming vodka bottles
The tank shifts it's turret over and fires.
The shell screams towards my knockoff Maginot Line, and obliterates a nest
My men start yelling in sheer horror at the loss of comrades and their approaching doom
I'm pounding on my desk for the anti-tank guns to hurry the hell up.
And then.. the German infantry charges in.. with the Tiger supporting them.
Knowing my men are doomed. And the defence is lost.. I decide to make one last charge.
"OOOOOOOORRRRRRRRAAAAAAHHHHHH!!!!!!!"
The conscripts all pile out of the trenches and charge towards the advancing Germans, rifles in the air and Mother Russia in their hearts
The Germans yell commands and hold position. Then open fire
Conscripts fall left right and center, but still they press on. The Glorious Last Charge
The German machine guns cannot defeat them all.. Or so I think..
Then.. I hear engines.. Many. Engines.
MY ALLY! He saw my doom and brought forth T-34's and Guards!
The Germans shift fire and fall back. They've been outflanked.
I yell into my mic to press the attack, but my ally says no.
"Why?" I ask.
"Just watch." He replies. So I watch
The Germans retreat to the bridge. Back to their defensive lines.
Then. I notice it. The bridge is littered with explosive charges.
My ally laughs maniacally and the bridge goes up like a nuclear explosion, sending shrapnel, debris and bodies everywhere
My FPS drops to 10.
As the dust settles, the bridge is gone. The German advance is gone.
I cry out in victorious praise! The day is saved!
And then all of a sudden.. I hear that dreaded first shot. The deafening *BOOM* in the distance.
The Germans called in the Railway Artillery...
Their advance hadn't been stopped... It was just a diversion..
10/10 I love this game.
